docs.title: spa2mqtt
docs.text:
spa2mqtt connects the RS485 bus of a Balboa-family "encrypted" hot-tub controller to Home Assistant. RS485 is the two-wire serial bus that the tub's control board uses to talk to its topside panel. The Jacuzzi J235 is the first supported tub. Related Jacuzzi and Sundance boards use the same protocol family. The MQTT bridge also reads one unencrypted Jacuzzi, the J345, through its ProLink module.

You can run it in two ways. Both use the same tub definitions, so both give the same entities in Home Assistant.

MQTT bridge ESPHome component Runs on Any Docker host (Python) An ESP32 with an RS485 transceiver Connects to the tub through An RS485-to-TCP adapter such as the EW11A, or a USB RS485 adapter The ESP32's own UART Talks to Home Assistant through An MQTT broker, with MQTT discovery The ESPHome native API Install guide Docker Compose or Portainer ESPHome spa2mqtt architecture The spa control board RS485 header connects either to an EW11A RS485-to-TCP adapter that feeds the spa2mqtt Docker container, which publishes to an MQTT broker read by Home Assistant, or to an ESP32 running the ESPHome spa_bus component, which talks to Home Assistant over the ESPHome native API. Spa control board RS485 header for a second topside panel EW11A RS485 to TCP, port 8899 spa2mqtt Python, Docker MQTT broker e.g. Mosquitto ESP32 + RS485 ESPHome, spa_bus Home Assistant same entities Option A: MQTT bridge Option B: ESPHome (no extra box) TCP MQTT ESPHome native API RS485 A/B

Mains voltage

A spa contains mains voltage and can deliver a large fault current. Isolate the spa at its breaker before you open any panel. Wiring anything into it is at your own risk. Read Safety before you start.

docs.title: Receive-only by default
docs.text: spa2mqtt never transmits to the tub unless you enable transmit. With transmit off, it only listens, so a wrong setting or a wrong tub definition cannot change the tub. Buttons and the temperature setpoint still appear in Home Assistant, but they show as unavailable. See Safety for what changes when you enable transmit.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
1. Read Getting started. It helps you choose between the MQTT bridge and ESPHome, and it shows a read-only first run.
  2. Install with Docker Compose, Portainer or ESPHome.
  3. Look up settings in Configuration.

docs.title: Supported tubs
docs.text:
Model Board Definition Status Jacuzzi J235 (2018) Encrypted (C4/CC frames) jacuzzi_j235 Sensors confirmed against labelled captures. The transmit path is tested against a simulated board, not yet against the tub. See the J235 guide. Jacuzzi J345 (J-300 series) Plain (0x16 frames) via the ProLink module jacuzzi_j345 MQTT bridge only. Decoded from the owner's captures; transmit reproduces captured pyjacuzzi frames; not yet run against the tub by this project. See the J345 guide.

To add your tub, see Monitor and capture and Tub definitions.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This page lists every setting of the MQTT bridge. The ESPHome component has its own settings in the device YAML. See ESPHome.

docs.title: Where settings come from
docs.text:
The bridge reads settings from two places:

  1. config.yml. A YAML file. The container reads /app/config.yml. Outside Docker, spa2mqtt run reads config.yml in the current folder, or the file given with -c FILE. The file is optional. Without it, the bridge uses the defaults and the environment variables. Start from config.yml.example.
  2. Environment variables. They cover the settings that change from one install to the next. An environment variable overrides the same setting in config.yml.

An empty environment variable counts as unset, with one exception: SPA_TRANSMIT. If SPA_TRANSMIT exists at all, it decides transmit, and an empty value means false. This can only switch transmit off, never on, so it fails safe.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable config.yml key Default Meaning SPA_IP spa.transport.host 192.168.1.100 Address of the RS485-to-TCP adapter, or of the ProLink module SPA_PORT spa.transport.port 8899 TCP port of the adapter. 4257 for a ProLink module SPA_DEFINITION spa.definition jacuzzi_j235 Tub definition ID, alias or file path. See Tub definitions VARIANT_DEFINITION spa.definition v1 name of SPA_DEFINITION. SPA_DEFINITION wins if both are set SPA_TRANSMIT spa.transmit false Allow commands to the tub. See Transmit MQTT_BROKER mqtt.broker localhost MQTT broker address MQTT_PORT mqtt.port 1883 MQTT broker port MQTT_USERNAME mqtt.username none Broker user name MQTT_PASSWORD mqtt.password none Broker password LOG_LEVEL log_level INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR

Boolean values accept true, 1, yes and on (any case). Every other value means false.

The Compose files also use SPA2MQTT_TAG to choose the image tag. The bridge itself does not read it. See Releases and versions.

docs.title: ha
docs.text:
These keys control how the bridge appears in Home Assistant. MQTT discovery is the Home Assistant feature that creates entities from retained config messages on the broker.

Key Default Meaning ha.discovery_prefix homeassistant Discovery prefix that Home Assistant listens on ha.base_topic spa2mqtt First part of the state and command topics, for example spa2mqtt/jacuzzi_j235/... ha.device_name From the tub definition Device name in Home Assistant. With legacy_topics, it is also part of the discovery topics. Jacuzzi J235 for jacuzzi_j235, Jacuzzi J345 for jacuzzi_j345 ha.device_identifier From the tub definition Device identifier. For jacuzzi_j235 it is 185569045, the device that the v1 bridge created, so an upgrade keeps it. For jacuzzi_j345 it is jacuzzi_j345 ha.unique_id_prefix empty Text put in front of every entity unique_id. See unique_id_prefix ha.legacy_topics true Publish discovery to the topics that v1 used. See Legacy topics ha.heartbeat 60 Seconds between re-publishes of unchanged values ha.heartbeat_overrides none Per-field heartbeat, as field: seconds

The two device keys default to the tub definition's ha: section, or to its name and id. An install that sets only environment variables therefore gets the right device for its tub. For the J235 nothing changes. A custom definition file that relied on the old fixed defaults (Jacuzzi J235, 185569045) now gets its own name and ID: set both keys in config.yml, or add an ha: section to the definition, to keep the old device.

docs.title: Transmit
docs.text:
Transmit is off by default. With transmit off:

  • The bridge never writes to the bus.
  • Buttons and the setpoint number still appear in Home Assistant, so their identities stay the same. They show as unavailable.
  • Commands that reach the bridge anyway are dropped with a warning in the log.

With transmit on:

  • The log shows TRANSMIT ENABLED at start-up.
  • The bridge still sends nothing at start-up.
  • On the first command from Home Assistant, it claims a client channel on the bus, the same way a second topside panel does. Then it sends the button press.
  • For a setpoint change, it presses up or down one step at a time and checks the status after each press, until the setpoint matches the target.

A tub definition with bus.mode: direct (the J345 behind a ProLink module) has no channel to claim. On the first command after each connection the bridge sends one connection-check frame, and then one frame per command, about 1.2 seconds apart. A setpoint change is one frame, not a series of presses, and nothing is retried. See the J345 guide.

Read Safety before you enable transmit.

docs.title: unique_id_prefix
docs.text:
Home Assistant uses each entity's unique_id to remember its entity ID, name and area. The default empty prefix gives bare IDs such as current_temperature. These are the IDs that the v1 bridge used, so an upgrade from v1 keeps every entity.

On a fresh install, set a prefix such as spa_ if another MQTT integration could use the same bare IDs. Two entities with the same unique_id cannot both exist. Choose the prefix before the first start: a change later creates new entities and leaves the old ones behind.

docs.title: Legacy topics
docs.text:
The v1 bridge published discovery messages to <discovery_prefix>/<component>/<device_name>/<entity_name>/config, with unsafe characters replaced by -. Discovery messages are retained on the broker. With legacy_topics: true, the bridge publishes to those same topics, so it replaces the old retained messages in place. Without that, Home Assistant would keep the v1 config as well and could show duplicate entities.

Keep the default if you upgrade from v1. On a fresh install the setting does no harm. Because the topic contains device_name and the entity name, changing either one moves the discovery topic.

docs.title: Upgrade from v1
docs.text:
The v1 bridge is kept on the legacy/pre-rewrite branch. Version 2 is built to replace it in place:

  • Your v1 config.yml keeps working. The keys in the table below and the environment variables SPA_IP, SPA_PORT, VARIANT_DEFINITION and MQTT_* are still read.
  • Home Assistant identities stay the same: the same device (185569045), the same unique_ids, and discovery on the same topics. Retained configs are replaced in place, and entity IDs do not change.
  • Behaviour change: buttons and Temperature Set Control are unavailable until you enable transmit. v1 transmitted by default.
  • State topics move from hmd/... to spa2mqtt/jacuzzi_j235/.... Home Assistant follows the change through discovery, so you do nothing.
  • New entities: Pump 1 Speed, Light Button, the Pump 1, Pump 1 Low, Pump 2 and Light switches, Light Mode, and diagnostics that are disabled by default.
  • The Pump 1 switch is the jets (pump 1 on high). Pump 1 Low is the low speed the board also runs by itself to heat or filter; while it does, Pump 1 Low may not turn off.
  • Main Pump Status is pump 1 on high. Circulation Pump Status is pump 1 running at any speed, because the J235 circulates on pump 1 low.

Stop the v1 container before you start version 2. v1 transmits at start-up, and the adapter may accept only one TCP client.

docs.title: spa2mqtt v2: design
docs.text: Status: plan, written before implementation (phase 2). Deviations found during implementation are recorded in §11 and in the pull request.

docs.title: 1. Goals and non-goals
docs.text:
Goals

  1. Keep the deployed architecture: RS485 ↔ tub, MQTT ↔ Home Assistant, as a Docker container talking to an RS485-to-TCP bridge (EW11A).
  2. Separate the code into layers with one direction of dependency: transport → protocol codec → tub model → HA/MQTT.
  3. Config-driven tubs. A new tub model is a data file (YAML, validated by a JSON Schema). No Python or C++ is needed unless it uses a framing or cipher family that does not exist yet.
  4. A native ESPHome external component that consumes the same definition files, so the ESP32 exposes the same controls and sensors over the ESPHome API.
  5. Keep the HA identities the current stack uses (unique_ids, device, entity IDs).
  6. Tests that replay the captured dumps, plus lint, type checks and CI.

Non-goals (this PR)

  • Filter-cycle programming, menu automation, climate entity, light colour selection. The definition schema can express them later; there is no J235 evidence for them yet (protocol.md §9). Since §10 row 16 the J235 light is an on/off switch with its mode shown.
  • Unencrypted (0x16) Jacuzzi boards on a direct RS485 tap, and on ESPHome. Since §11 row 12 the bridge supports one such tub, the J345, through its ProLink module only (protocol: jacuzzi_plain, protocol-plain.md). The legacy jacuzzi_j335_unencrypted_* debug definitions were not ported (debug-only, unverified, wrong message type): the J345 definition was written from the captures.

docs.title: 2. Safety model (transmit)
docs.text:
The single most important design rule: nothing transmits unless explicitly enabled.

  • Both implementations have a transmit setting, default false. With it off, the transport is never written to; the code path that would write raises (Python) or returns early and logs (C++).
  • All bus writes go through one choke point, marked # TRANSMITS / // TRANSMITS:
  • Python: BusWriter.send() in spa2mqtt/tub/bus.py.
  • C++: SpaBus::transmit_frame_() in spa_bus.cpp.
  • A test asserts that no other module calls Transport.write.
  • No transmission at start-up. The legacy bridge claims a channel (0x01/0x03) automatically; the new code only claims a channel lazily, when the first command is queued and transmit is on.
  • With transmit: false, command entities (buttons, setpoint number) are still announced, so HA identities stay intact, but they report as unavailable and commands are dropped with a warning.
  • Development and CI use only replayed captures and an in-process mock board.

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
┌───────────────── spa2mqtt (Python, Docker) ──────────────────┐
 RS485 ── EW11A ─► transport ─► protocol ─► tub ─────────► ha ──► MQTT ──► HA
          (TCP)    tcp/serial/   framing,    decoder,      discovery,
                   replay        crc, cipher state, bus,   bridge
                                             setpoint
                       ▲                        ▲
                       └──── definitions/*.yaml (JSON Schema) ────┐
                                                                  │ read at compile time
                ┌──────────── ESPHome external component ─────────┴──────────┐
 RS485 ── UART ─► SpaBus (C++): FrameDecoder → fold → field table → entities ─► ESPHome API ─► HA
                  generated from the definition by esphome/components/spa_bus/__init__.py
                └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 3.1 Python module layout
docs.text:
spa2mqtt/
  __main__.py            CLI: run | replay | decode | validate
  app.py                 composition root (builds the layers from config)
  config.py              runtime config (YAML + env vars, legacy keys accepted)
  transport/
    base.py              Transport protocol: async read_chunk(); write() (guarded)
    tcp.py               TCP client with reconnect/backoff (EW11A)
    serial.py            optional direct serial (pyserial-asyncio extra)
    replay.py            replays '<epoch> RX <hex>' capture logs; refuses write()
  protocol/
    crc.py               CRC-8 0x07/0x02/0x02
    framing.py           streaming FrameDecoder, encode_frame()
    frame.py             Frame dataclass (addr, mid, type, payload)
    cipher.py            fold(), cc_encode()/cc_decode()
  definitions/
    model.py             typed dataclasses (TubDefinition, FieldDef, EntityDef, …)
    loader.py            resolve name/alias/path → validate (jsonschema + semantics) → model
  tub/
    decoder.py           status payload → {field: value} using FieldDef transforms
    state.py             TubState: last values, change detection, timestamps
    bus.py               BusClient state machine (LISTEN/CLAIM/REQUESTED/READY), BusWriter,
                         DirectBusClient (fixed address, no claim: plain boards via ProLink)
    control.py           CommandQueue, SetpointController (press loop with retries)
  ha/
    discovery.py         pure functions: definition + install config → discovery payloads
    bridge.py            paho-mqtt client: publish config/state/availability, route commands
definitions/
  tub-definition.schema.json
  jacuzzi_j235.yaml
  jacuzzi_j345.yaml      plain protocol, bridge only
esphome/
  components/spa_bus/    __init__.py, sensor.py, binary_sensor.py, button.py, number.py,
                         text_sensor.py, spa_bus.{h,cpp}, spa_protocol.{h,cpp} (framework-free)
  example-jacuzzibridge-esp.yaml
tools/
  capture.py             receive-only raw capture (never writes)
  research/              analysis scripts behind docs/protocol.md
tests/
  fixtures/captures/     raw/*.log, decoded/*.csv (ground truth)
  test_*.py              unit + replay tests
  cpp/                   host-compiled tests of spa_protocol.cpp against the same fixtures

Dependencies: PyYAML, paho-mqtt>=2, jsonschema. Optional: pyserial-asyncio. ha-mqtt-discoverable is dropped. It hid the topic scheme, forced pydantic, and the bridge needs exact control of topics to keep HA identities (§8).

docs.title: 3.2 Data flow (Python)
docs.text:
1. The transport yields byte chunks.
  2. FrameDecoder resynchronises on 7E, frames by LEN, checks the CRC and yields Frames.
  3. BusClient sees every frame (CTS/CC bookkeeping). Status frames whose type matches the definition go to the decoder, which applies fold and the field transforms.
  4. TubState.update() returns the fields that changed.
  5. ha.bridge publishes changed values immediately. Unchanged values are re-published every heartbeat seconds (default 60, per-entity overrides), as the legacy sensor_update_intervals did.
  6. HA commands go through ha.bridge → tub.control (button press / setpoint target) → CommandQueue → BusClient sends on the next CTS for our channel (if transmit is enabled).

docs.title: 4. Tub-definition schema
docs.text:
One YAML file per tub model in definitions/, validated by definitions/tub-definition.schema.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12) plus semantic checks in the loader (referenced fields/buttons exist, byte offsets within the payload length, unique keys). Sketch:

schema_version: 1
id: jacuzzi_j235
aliases: [jacuzzi_j235_encrypted]       # legacy config name keeps working
name: Jacuzzi J235
manufacturer: Jacuzzi
model: J235
protocol: balboa_encrypted              # codec family implemented in code
temperature_unit: C

bus:                                    # only used when transmit is enabled
  baud: 115200
  client_mid: 0xBF
  channel_request_magic: [0xF1, 0x73]
  dormant_channel_threshold: 5

status:
  type: 0xC4
  decode: fold                          # fold | unkey | decrypt (J235 today) | plain (jacuzzi_plain)
  length: 16                            # decoded payload bytes

commands:
  type: 0xCC
  encode: cc_xor                        # [K, K ^ 0xE0 ^ code]
  buttons: {temp_up: 0x01, temp_down: 0x02, pump_1: 0x04, pump_2: 0x05}

fields:                                 # decoded-payload field map
  water_temperature: {byte: 5, xor: 0x02, scale: 0.5, status: confirmed, evidence: "protocol.md §5 d5"}
  setpoint:          {byte: 8, scale: 0.5, status: inferred}
  heater:            {byte: 10, bit: 6, status: inferred}
  hour:              {byte: 0, xor: 0x06, status: confirmed}

entities:
  - key: current_temperature            # stable key = HA unique_id suffix (legacy: whole id)
    component: sensor                   # sensor | binary_sensor | button | number | text_sensor | switch
    field: water_temperature
    name: Current Water Temperature
    device_class: temperature
    unit_of_measurement: "°C"
    state_class: measurement
    icon: mdi:coolant-temperature
  - key: pump_1_button
    component: button
    press: pump_1
  - key: temperature_set_control
    component: number
    field: setpoint
    control: {type: stepper, up: temp_up, down: temp_down}
    min: 20
    max: 40
    step: 0.5
    mode: slider

Field transform (identical in Python and C++, golden-tested across both):

raw = big-endian integer of decoded[byte : byte + length]      (length default 1)
raw = raw ^ xor                                                 (default 0)
if bit is set:    value = (raw >> bit) & 1           → bool
else:             raw   = (raw >> shift) & mask      (defaults 0, all ones)
                  if raw in invalid: value = None
                  elif map:  value = map[raw]  (unknown raw → None, warn once)
                  else:      value = raw * scale + offset       (defaults 1, 0)

Every field carries status: confirmed | inferred | hypothesis, mirroring protocol.md. The bridge logs hypothesis-backed entities at start-up. An entity may set enabled_by_default: false (used for new diagnostics, not for the legacy set).

What needs code vs data. A new tub that speaks balboa_encrypted with a different field map, button set, or entity list needs only a YAML file. A new framing or cipher family needs a codec in protocol/ and spa_protocol.cpp. The protocol key selects it, and an unknown value fails validation.

config.yml (or env vars). Install-specific settings live here, not in the definition:

  definition: jacuzzi_j235          # legacy key `config:` accepted
  transport: {type: tcp, host: 192.168.1.100, port: 8899}   # legacy spa.connection.* accepted
  transmit: false                   # MUST be set true to send any command
mqtt: {broker: …, port: 1883, username: …, password: …}

  discovery_prefix: homeassistant
  device_name: Jacuzzi J235
  device_identifier: "185569045"    # legacy device id, keeps the HA device
  unique_id_prefix: ""              # "" = legacy bare unique_ids (default)

docs.title: 6. Bus state machine and setpoint control
docs.text:
Implemented as in protocol.md §4, with these choices:

  • LISTEN always; it records known_channels (CTS targets) and active_channels (CC sources).
  • A channel is claimed only when the command queue is non-empty and transmit is on.
  • Dormant-channel reuse is tried first, then a 0x01 request on the next 0x00.
  • A CC seen from another device on our channel drops back to LISTEN (conflict).
  • SetpointController: target clamped to entity min/max and rounded to step. On each status frame:
  • If |setpoint − target| < step/2, done.
  • Otherwise, at most one press is in flight. Press up or down, then wait for confirm_frames (default 3) status frames.
  • If the setpoint did not move, retry. Give up after max_attempts (default 40, enough for 20 °C of travel), logged.
  • A topside change during the loop is respected: a new HA target replaces the old one, and no automatic re-assertion happens after completion. This replaces the legacy approach of queueing N presses at once and assuming each one lands.
  • Buttons enqueue a single press. There is no de-duplication; HA buttons are momentary.
  • ToggleController (switch entities): the target is on or off. On each status frame:
  • If the field equals the target, done. No press is sent when it already does. With an off_field, "off" is reached when that field reads false instead (pump 1 low → high is not off).
  • Otherwise, at most one press is in flight. Press, then wait confirm_frames (default 10) status frames for the field to follow. A change in progress_field (a pump speed) ends the wait at once: the press landed, and the cycle needs another.
  • Give up after max_presses (default 3), logged. The J235 board keeps pump 1 low while it heats or filters, so "Pump 1 Low" off can be impossible. "Pump 1" (the jets) reads pump 1 high only, so the board's own low speed does not show it on.

Direct bus mode (bus.mode: direct, protocol-plain.md §6–§7). A ProLink module's TCP stream has no CTS, so DirectBusClient replaces the claim logic for jacuzzi_plain definitions:

  • Frames are sent from the fixed bus.client_address. There is no channel state.
  • The queue holds whole frames (button presses and direct commands), at most 8.
  • One frame is released per send_gap_frames status frames. Only status frames count, so the spacing follows the tub's own cadence.
  • bus.hello, when set, is sent once per connection, immediately before the first queued frame. Nothing is sent at start-up.
  • Tub.on_connect() (called by the app after each transport connect) clears the queue and re-arms the hello, so a command queued before an outage is not sent after it.
  • A number with control.type: direct is one frame with the value rounded to step. A value outside min..max is refused, not clamped. There is no SetpointController and no retry: pyjacuzzi sent each command once, and all took.
  • A switch is one frame, sent only when the field differs from the target. The loader requires max_presses: 1.
  • A direct command may carry requires (status bit fields and the value each must have). Tub refuses the command (CommandBlocked) when the last status frame disagrees or none has been decoded. The J345 uses it to block the setpoint in Celsius mode.
  • Both clients hand frames to the same BusWriter, which stays the only writer.

docs.title: 7. ESPHome component (spa_bus)
docs.text:
Native, no Docker sidecar. Everything the bridge does fits on an ESP32: UART at 115200, 40-byte frames, a CRC table, a 16-byte field decode, a small state machine. IR proves the same workload on an ESP32 for Sundance boards. There is nothing that needs a sidecar.

external_components:
  - source: github://srleach/spa2mqtt@main
    components: [spa_bus]
uart:
  id: spa_uart
  tx_pin: GPIO17
  rx_pin: GPIO18
  baud_rate: 115200
spa_bus:
  id: spa
  uart_id: spa_uart
  definition: jacuzzi_j235        # name/alias from definitions/, or a path to a YAML file
  transmit: false                 # default; buttons/number unavailable when false
  # flow_control_pin: GPIOxx      # RS485 DE/RE if the transceiver needs it
sensor:
  - platform: spa_bus
    entity: current_temperature   # key from the definition
    name: Current Water Temperature

Sharing the definitions. external_components clones the whole repository, so the component's Python code (__init__.py) reads definitions/<name>.yaml from the clone at compile time. It validates the file with the same schema (the jsonschema package if available, otherwise structural checks; the full validation runs in CI) and generates C++ calls that load the field table, button codes and entity bindings into SpaBus:

spa->add_field(5, 1, 0x02, 0, 0xFF, -1, 0.5f, 0.0f);   // water_temperature
spa->add_button("pump_1", 0x04);

Platforms reference definition entities by entity: key. Final validation checks that the key exists and that its component matches the platform. Default name, device_class, unit, icon, state_class and entity_category come from the definition, so a minimal YAML only needs entity:. To avoid hand-writing a dozen entries, a generated package esphome/packages/<definition>.yaml lists every entity of a definition. tools/gen_esphome_package.py regenerates it, and CI fails if it is stale.

C++ structure.

  • spa_protocol.{h,cpp}: framework-free (no ESPHome headers). CRC, FrameDecoder, fold, CC encode, field decode. Compiled on the host in CI and run against the same fixtures as the Python tests (golden JSON produced by the Python decoder).
  • spa_bus.{h,cpp}: the ESPHome Component + UARTDevice. Reads the UART in loop(), owns the bus state machine, the command queue, the setpoint controller, and the entity bindings.
  • Entities: SpaSensor, SpaBinarySensor, SpaButton, SpaNumber, plus a diagnostic text_sensor (bus state: listening / claiming / ready / tx disabled).
  • Entities publish on change plus a heartbeat (default 60 s). Command entities are marked unavailable when transmit: false.

docs.title: 8. HA identity preservation and migration
docs.text:
MQTT bridge (drop-in replacement).

  • Same device: identifiers 185569045, name Jacuzzi J235. Manufacturer/model are corrected to Jacuzzi/J235; HA updates those in place.
  • Same unique_ids: bare entity keys (current_temperature, heater_active, …).
  • Same discovery config topics as ha-mqtt-discoverable: homeassistant/<component>/Jacuzzi-J235/<clean(name)>/config with clean = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "-", s). The new retained config replaces the old one in place, so there is no duplicate-unique_id conflict and no orphaned retained message.
  • State and command topics move from hmd/<component>/Jacuzzi-J235/<Name>/… to spa2mqtt/<device>/<key>/{state,set} plus a shared availability topic. The config payload announces them, so HA follows automatically. Old hmd/… state topics are not retained by the legacy code (except availability), so nothing is left over.
  • Entity IDs are unchanged, because HA keys the registry by unique_id. Behavioural change: buttons and the setpoint number are unavailable until spa.transmit: true is set.

ESPHome (optional, later). The ESPHome device is a new HA device. If its friendly_name is Jacuzzi J235, ESPHome generates the same entity IDs (sensor.jacuzzi_j235_current_water_temperature, …). The switch-over is therefore:

  1. Stop the bridge.
  2. Delete the MQTT device in HA, so the entity IDs are released.
  3. Flash and adopt the ESP.

Long-term statistics follow the entity ID. The example YAML uses friendly_name: Jacuzzi J235 for this reason.

Rollback. The legacy code is preserved on branch legacy/pre-rewrite (b0a5323). The legacy config.yml keys keep working, so rolling back is a container image change.

docs.title: 9. Test strategy
docs.text:
Layer Tests Fixtures CRC / framing known-good frames, corrupted CRC, split chunks, junk between frames, 0x7E inside payload, oversize LEN D1 raw frames; synthetic Cipher fold on D1 equals expected; fold ⇔ key-stream identity; CC encode/decode on the SC example frame D1, SC/HJ frames Field decode every decoded CSV row decodes; clock fields match filename wall-clock; timeline assertions (heater on rows 1–51, circulation rows 1–277, idle afterwards) D2–D6 Replay end-to-end raw D1 through the full pipeline → expected HA states; CSVs re-encoded to frames with random keys (marked synthetic) → identical decode D1–D6 Definitions every definitions/*.yaml validates; J235 entity keys ⊇ HA entity set; semantic checks fail on broken examples – HA discovery snapshot of every config payload (topic, unique_id, device, command/state topics) – Bus / control mock board: no write ever with transmit off; dormant-channel claim; request/ack; setpoint loop converges, retries, gives up; conflict handling in-process mock C++ core host build of spa_protocol.cpp; decode every fixture frame and compare with Python's golden JSON same fixtures ESPHome esphome config on the example; esphome compile in CI (slow job) example YAML

Tooling: ruff (lint and format), mypy --strict on spa2mqtt/, pytest, GitHub Actions jobs python, cpp, esphome.

docs.title: 10. Decisions log
docs.text: # Decision Why 1 ~~Canonical decode is the pairwise fold (Model B)~~, superseded by §11 row 11 (per-byte decryption). Key-independent; correct calendar day on J235; equals the legacy definition offsets, so identities and history are unaffected (protocol.md §3.2). 2 Drop ha-mqtt-discoverable; use paho directly. Needed exact topic control for identity preservation; fewer dependencies (pydantic). 3 transmit defaults to false in both implementations. User constraint and bus safety; the legacy code transmitted at start-up. 4 Lazy channel claim. Never touch the bus unless a command needs it. 5 Keep hypothesis-backed legacy entities (main/secondary pump, manual circulation). They are the minimum set HA uses today. They are flagged status: hypothesis and documented. 6 Definitions are YAML with a JSON Schema in the repo root definitions/. Human-editable; one source for Python and ESPHome codegen. 7 ESPHome entities are declared by entity: key plus a generated package, rather than auto-created by the hub. Idiomatic ESPHome (users can rename, filter, hide); explicit IDs; still zero duplication via the package. 8 Legacy unencrypted J335 definitions are not ported. Debug-only, unverified, used the wrong message type for plain boards. The J345 definition (§11 row 12) was written from captures instead. 9 Temperature unit is configuration, not decoded. No unit flag is known on encrypted boards (protocol.md §8). 10 Wire format for captures is <epoch> RX <hex> / MARK. Same file from the capture tool, the replay transport, and the tests. 11 A tub nobody on the project can test may transmit only frames a capture shows working. Every button and direct command carries a status and evidence, and a test enumerates what the definition can emit. The J345 is driven on the strength of its owner's pyjacuzzi capture. A decode error shows a wrong value; a wrong frame acts on someone else's tub. 12 The Home Assistant device name and identifier default from the tub definition (ha:, else name and id). The J235 pins 185569045 in its YAML. Environment-only installs (Portainer on Home Assistant OS) cannot set ha: keys, and a second tub must not appear as "Jacuzzi J235". 13 A text_sensor is published to Home Assistant as a sensor. The bridge clears the retained config it used to publish under text_sensor. Home Assistant's MQTT discovery has no text_sensor component, so Pump 1 Speed and Light Mode never appeared. text_sensor stays in definitions because it is the ESPHome platform name. 14 Pump switches are new entities next to the pump buttons, and they are bridge-only. The buttons keep their keys and names, so no Home Assistant entity changes. The ESPHome component would need a new platform and a second controller in the C++ core; the package generator leaves switches out until then. 15 spa2mqtt capture compares keyed frames after removing the key, and writes the capture file format. The J235 re-keys every status, lights and panel frame, so a byte comparison would suppress nothing. A dump that replays needs no second parser. 16 J235 Pump 1 reads pump 1 high (jets); a new Pump 1 Low switch covers the low speed, with off_field: pump_1_running. The J235 lights frame (CA) is an extra frame with decode: fold, giving a Light switch and Light Mode. Extra-frame entities are bridge only. Pump 1 on "running at any speed" came back on whenever the board started pump 1 low to heat or filter, and the low speed had no control. The ESPHome component decodes the status frame only, so its loader and the package generator leave extra-frame fields out.

docs.title: 11. Deviations from this plan
docs.text: # Deviation Why 1 Mid-implementation, the owner's labelled raw capture (D7) arrived. The J235 definition gained pump_1_speed (text sensor), light_button, set_mode, and two disabled-by-default diagnostics. Internal field names were renamed to their confirmed meaning (pump_1_running, pump_1_high). Entity keys and names were unchanged. Evidence over folklore (protocol.md §5). HA identities untouched. 2 Channel acquisition: the 0x00/0x01 request is the primary path; dormant-channel reuse is kept as a fallback. D7 shows the topside answers every CTS on the only polled channel, so there is never a dormant channel on this install. 3 SetpointController waits for movement instead of counting presses. D7: the first press only enters set mode. The planned loop already tolerated this; tests now model it explicitly (mock board). 4 ESPHome command entities cannot be marked unavailable individually. With transmit: false they log a warning and do nothing, and the optional bus_state text sensor reads receive-only. ESPHome entities have no per-entity availability. The MQTT bridge does mark them unavailable. 5 The ESPHome definition.py loader uses jsonschema only when installed (ESPHome does not ship it) and otherwise does structural checks. CI validates every definition with the full schema. Avoid forcing an extra dependency into users' ESPHome environments. 6 SpaCore (definition tables + decoder + bus + setpoint loop) lives in the framework-free header, and SpaBus is a thin ESPHome wrapper. Lets the host test drive the exact production state machine, not a copy. 7 Docker image build is verified in CI only. No Docker daemon in the development sandbox. 9 Set-mode awareness: control.set_mode_field names the bit that shows the topside's set screen. The controller treats a press that opens set mode as the wake press and steps on the next frame. It also no longer counts down while its press is still queued for a bus slot. protocol.md §7a. The queued-press guard fixes a real overshoot found by the new tests (a slow channel grant caused duplicate presses). Ported to the C++ core. 11 Status decoding moved from the pairwise fold to per-byte decryption (status.decode: decrypt with a keystream). Fields read plaintext with no per-field XOR. Legacy fold-only logs are rebuilt through status.fold_template. Raw captures showed the fold loses data when both bytes of a pair change (protocol.md §3.3). The fix also makes the field map portable to Sundance boards. It supersedes decision 1. 10 spa2mqtt monitor: a standalone, read-only live decoder for the terminal (text or JSON lines, optional raw recording). The owner's first contact with the real tub runs without MQTT and without any transmit path. 8 ~~Unencrypted Jacuzzi captures from unmerged PR 12 were recovered into tests/fixtures/captures/unencrypted/ but are not decoded.~~ Superseded by row 12. They evidenced the plain codec non-goal; no J235 relevance. 12 The plain protocol is supported for one tub, the Jacuzzi J345 behind a ProLink module: protocol: jacuzzi_plain, status.decode: plain, a second decoded frame (extra_frames, lights 0x23), commands.direct, and bus.mode: direct. Bridge only: the ESPHome loader rejects the protocol and the package generator skips it. No C++ changed. A contributor's tub, with five captures that include a pyjacuzzi session of working commands. The ProLink stream has no CTS, so the claim logic cannot send to it.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page helps you choose how to run spa2mqtt and shows a safe first run. The first run only reads the bus. It proves that your wiring and your tub definition work before anything can send a command to the tub.

docs.title: 1. Choose how to run it
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Do you already run an MQTT broker<br/>and a Docker host near the tub?] -->|Yes| B[Do you have an RS485-to-TCP adapter<br/>such as an EW11A?]
    A -->|No| E[ESPHome on an ESP32]
    B -->|Yes| M[MQTT bridge in Docker]
    B -->|No| C[Do you want one small device<br/>with no extra server?]
    C -->|Yes| E
    C -->|No| M

MQTT bridge (Docker). Choose this if you already have an RS485-to-TCP adapter, such as the EW11A, wired to the tub. The bridge is easy to update and to debug, because it runs as a normal container and logs to the console. It needs an MQTT broker, for example the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant.

ESPHome. Choose this if you want one small device in the tub cabinet and no extra server. The ESP32 decodes the bus itself and talks to Home Assistant over the ESPHome native API. You do not need an MQTT broker. See ESPHome.

You can start with one and move to the other later. Both use the same tub definitions and the same entity names. See Switch over from MQTT.

docs.title: 2. What you need
docs.text:
For both options:

  • A supported tub. Today that is the Jacuzzi J235 (jacuzzi_j235, see the J235 guide), and, with the MQTT bridge only, the Jacuzzi J345 (jacuzzi_j345). Other tubs need a tub definition.
  • Access to the RS485 header on the spa control board. The header is intended for a second topside panel. It carries the RS485 A and B lines that the topside panel uses.
  • A way to isolate the spa from mains power while you wire it. See Safety.

Jacuzzi J345 with a ProLink module

The J345 needs no wiring and no adapter: the bridge connects to the tub's ProLink module on TCP port 4257. Follow the J345 guide instead of the adapter steps on this page.

For the MQTT bridge:

  • An RS485-to-TCP adapter (for example the Elfin EW11A) set to 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1), in TCP server mode. spa2mqtt connects to it on port 8899 by default. A USB RS485 adapter also works if the container runs next to the tub.
  • A host that runs Docker, with Docker Compose or Portainer.
  • An MQTT broker that Home Assistant uses, with MQTT discovery enabled (the default).

For ESPHome:

  • An ESP32 board with an RS485 transceiver. The example uses a Waveshare ESP32-S3-ETH-8DI-8RO. See Hardware and wiring.

docs.title: 3. First run: read-only monitor
docs.text:
spa2mqtt monitor decodes the live bus and prints it to your terminal. It does not connect to MQTT and it cannot transmit. Three separate guards stop it from writing: the tub model runs receive-only, the monitor has no bus writer, and the connection is wrapped so that any write raises an error. Use it to check the wiring and the decoded values before you install anything else.

One client at a time

Many RS485-to-TCP adapters, the EW11A included, accept only one TCP client. Stop any other program that connects to the adapter first. An old v1 bridge must be stopped in any case, because v1 transmits at start-up.

Docker (no install)Python

Docker runs the published image once and removes the container when you press Ctrl-C. Replace the address with your adapter's address.

docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/srleach/spa2mqtt:2 spa2mqtt monitor 192.168.1.100

spa2mqtt needs Python 3.11 or later. A virtual environment keeps its packages apart from the rest of your system.

python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install "spa2mqtt @ git+https://github.com/srleach/spa2mqtt@v2.0.0"
spa2mqtt monitor 192.168.1.100

Replace v2.0.0 with the newest release tag. See Releases and versions. For a USB RS485 adapter, install spa2mqtt[serial] and use --serial /dev/ttyUSB0.

You get a full report at once, and then one every 10 seconds. Between reports, the monitor prints each value change and each topside button press as it happens.

Check these points against the topside panel:

  1. The water temperature matches the display.
  2. The clock (hour and minute) matches the topside clock.
  3. A pump or light press at the topside shows up as a change.
  4. The checksum error count stays at or near zero. A high count usually means a wrong baud rate or swapped A and B wires.

If all four are correct, the definition fits your tub. Continue with Docker Compose, Portainer or ESPHome. If they are wrong, see Monitor and capture and record a capture.

docs.title: 4. Next steps
docs.text:
• Leave transmit off for the first days. Watch the values in Home Assistant and compare them with the topside.
  • Enable transmit only when the values are right. See Safety and Configuration.
  • Pin a release so that updates happen when you choose. See Releases and versions.

docs.title: Project history: facts, findings and pivots
docs.text: A reconstruction of how spa2mqtt got here, written as source material for an engineering write-up. Dates come from git (author dates, Europe/London), GitHub PRs, the capture fixtures and the Home Assistant registry. Context that only the owner can supply (why a pivot happened) is marked (owner); everything else can be checked against the commits cited.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
• May 2025: two weeks of intense work turned a forked Sundance decoder into a Docker bridge (EW11A RS485-to-WiFi → MQTT → Home Assistant) for a Jacuzzi J235. Sensors worked; a few buttons worked "temporarily". Structure grew greedily around one tub, but with a stated goal of being pluggable for other Balboa-derived boards.
  • Mid 2025 to spring 2026: dormant. In April 2026 a two-day burst produced five refactor/fix PRs that were never merged; some of their "discovered fields" were wrong.
  • Autumn 2026 (owner): colder air means a bigger water-to-air ΔT, more heat loss, more "heat refill" and higher running costs. The tub has to be controlled, not just watched. At the same time the owner had an ESP32 board with RS485 on board, and found that the EW11 tries to phone home regularly with no way to turn it off. Hence ESPHome.
  • 4 November 2026: a full rebuild. The protocol was re-derived with citations. Both public "decryption" algorithms turned out to be the same cipher. A labelled raw capture from the tub confirmed or corrected every field the HA entities use. The bridge was rewritten around data-file tub definitions shared with a native ESPHome component.

docs.title: Prehistory: the shoulders stood on
docs.text: When What Why it matters 2017 → garbled1/pybalboa, ccutrer/balboa_worldwide_app: Balboa framing (0x7E, LEN, CRC-8 0x07) The CRC routine in every later project is garbled1's. 2023 HyperActiveJ decodes a Sundance 780 "encrypted" board: pairwise xormsg fold, C4 status, CC button codes 0xE1…, CTS channel squatting (sundance780-jacuzzi-balboa-rs485-tcp) The decode that spa2mqtt used, with magic constants "hour XOR 6" and "temp XOR 2". Mar 2023 – May 2024 David Holland-Moritz (dhmsjs/pyjacuzzi) decompiles the Prolink app. In Dec 2023 he adds encrypted-board support via a different algorithm: a key byte plus a mod-64 key stream. srleach forks it (65f4891). A second, apparently different, cipher model. Nobody had reconciled the two. 12 May 2025 srleach/SpaControl (8a56368 … ec631d8): HJ's sundanceRS485.py plus an MQTT control class, tweaked for "additional Jacuzzi idle screen" The first attempt: a working script, not a product.

docs.title: Phase 1: spa2mqtt v1 (15–27 May 2025)
docs.text:
Date Commit / PR Event 15 May 63057c3, 61c2564, ed63b6f, bd4618e, c221d22 Repo created; app stub; Docker; the first YAML tub config; "First Pass Conversion" from SpaControl. README concepts already say: "move all logic into dependencies … behaviours into config files … new tubs & board types can be added simply". 16 May PR 1 645e8b4 Message/packet abstraction. documentation/jacuzzi_encrypted/decoding.md records 54 raw C4 frames from the J235. These remained the only raw J235 frames until Nov 2026 (fixture D1). 18 May PR 3 9a4d005, PR 4 1c1c25e, PR 7 01516b6, PR 8 2755850 MQTT discovery via ha-mqtt-discoverable (bare unique_ids and the device 185569045 that HA still uses); J235 sensors (current/target temp, pump bits copied from Sundance code); maintenance sensors; change-driven publishing with heartbeat intervals; a debug harness writing decoded CSVs. 18 May d99bf10 First transmit code: "Introduce stub of sending pattern on CTS Receive". 18 May 6b19b0d First outside tub definition: a J335 unencrypted config from contributor @blackangel2109. Pluggability stops being hypothetical. 19–20 May a7348ce, 32049b2, 7442570, bb4c340, 59bc3b7 Debug logging to file (captures D2–D6); simulated communicator; split into base (plain) and jacuzzi_encrypted families loaded by class name from the YAML (family, communicator, spa). 21 May 240e570, ea21601; PR 12 (unmerged) CTS detection fix; sending flows stubbed. A contributor's unencrypted board captured through a Prolink on port 4257, including direct set-temperature (0x20) commands. Now in tests/fixtures/captures/unencrypted/. 25–27 May b302ddf, 81786f3, 32ffd0f, PR 14, PR 15 b0a5323 Button keymaps; "temporary buttons working state"; config clean-up. Last commit on main before this rebuild. The debug CSVs are deleted from the tree (d185ab1) and survive only in history.

State at the end of Phase 1. Temperature and setpoint were reliable. The pump bits were copied from Sundance code and never seen to change on the J235. Setpoint control pressed Temp up/down (target − current)/0.5 times. Start-up auto-claimed a bus channel, so the bridge could transmit without any user action. The architecture had pluggable intent, but the plumbing still contained a lot of J235 code paths.

docs.title: Phase 2: dormancy and the April 2026 burst
docs.text: Date Event Jun 2025 – Mar 2026 No commits. The bridge ran as-is. sometime before Nov 2026 Two entities, heater_active and manual_circulation_call, appear in HA under the same MQTT device. They are in no git ref, so they came from a local, unpushed definition. 9–10 Apr 2026 PRs 16–20 (b157d26, ebec593, fbf5cb5, b26e0ea, 1f7ebbb): a "protocol abstraction layer", a packet capture mode, "discovered fields", HA entity tweaks and unit tests. None were merged. Later shown to be wrong (Nov 2026): water temp needs no XOR; byte 10 is a pump map (it is heater plus flags); byte 14 is the hour (values 22–27 at 20:00).

docs.title: Phase 3: autumn 2026, the pivot to control and to ESPHome
docs.text:
Why (owner).

  1. Running cost. As outside temperature falls, ΔT between water and air rises, heat loss rises, and the heater "refills" heat more often. Reacting to that (scheduling setpoints, watching heater duty) needs reliable control and trustworthy heater/pump state. Display-only telemetry is not enough.
  2. Hardware. The owner acquired an ESP32 board with RS485 on board (HA holds an ESPHome config jacuzzibridge-esp for a Waveshare ESP32-S3-ETH-8DI-8RO; an archived config puts its RS485 UART on GPIO17/18).
  3. The EW11 phones home. The owner found that the EW11 RS485-to-WiFi bridge attempts to contact an external service regularly, with no apparent setting to disable it. A cloud-chatty black box on the tub's control bus is an unwelcome dependency. An ESP running ESPHome removes it and talks to HA natively.

The HA recorder shows the MQTT entities unavailable on 25 October 2026 and again on 4 November 2026.

docs.title: 4 November 2026: research
docs.text: Finding How it was established Consequence Captures in history git log --diff-filter=D found four deleted decoded CSVs; PR 12 had unencrypted captures Recovered into tests/fixtures/captures/ with ISO-dated names (the repo .gitignore had been hiding *.log/*-debug_messages.csv). CRC-8 is textbook garbled1's bit-by-bit "register 0xB5, augmented" routine equals poly 0x07, init 0x02, xorout 0x02 on every frame A 256-entry table in Python and C++. The "encryption" is a per-frame random key byte In D1 the first payload byte differs in 49 of 54 frames, yet payload ⊕ key is identical within a state The obfuscation is cosmetic. Both published decrypt models are the same cipher Algebra plus a check on all 54 frames: HJ fold d[j] = P[5+2j] ⊕ P[6+2j] of pyjacuzzi's plaintext; "hour XOR 6" is the key-stream constant; "temp XOR 2" and "minute ^0x08" are neighbouring constant bytes The magic constants are explained. The fold was chosen as canonical because it gave the right calendar day (16 May, the commit date) where pyjacuzzi's per-byte model gave 19 May. Upstream HJ independently reached the same identity. Tub clock vs wall clock Filename epochs of D3–D6 vs decoded hour/minute Hour/minute/day confirmed. The tub was on GMT, ~3 min fast, in May 2025. Heating curve D2: 37.5 → 38.0 → 38.5 around a 38.0 setpoint with the heater bit clearing The temp XOR stands. The April "no XOR" claim would mean a 2.5 °C jump in 10 minutes. Upstream drift HJ's repo was rewritten and redirected; its Jacuzzi 0x16 support was removed as "silently mis-decoded"; pyjacuzzi upstream added one temperature-scale commit (39c2834, 2026-11-03); Iraithium has a Sundance ESPHome component Confirms that 0x16 is plain (not J235). Proves ESP32 feasibility. Bus is 115200 8N1. Legacy code transmits at start-up Reading claim_channel_when_ready New safety rule: never transmit unless transmit: true, and never at start-up.

docs.title: 4 November 2026: the labelled capture (D7)
docs.text:
The owner ran tools/capture.py (receive-only; it has no socket write) against the EW11A and worked through a scripted list of topside actions, typing a label for each. Result: 9 minutes, 51 242 frames, 0 CRC errors, 37 labels.

Finding Evidence Only the topside (channel 0x10) is on the bus. It answers every CTS (~45 Hz) with a CC, code 0x00 when idle. A new-client poll 0x00 runs at ~1 Hz. C4 status at 3.3 Hz, CA lights at 1 Hz. Census No dormant channel exists, so HJ-style "squatting" cannot work on this install. Commands need the 0x00/0x01 channel request. Census Pump 1 is 2-speed: d2 bits 4–3 = off/low/high. d1 bit 6 = pump 1 running (the J235 circulates on pump 1 low). Pump 2 = d1 bit 2. Presses at t≈90/119/143/181/196 The legacy entities' bits were right; their names were broader than their meaning ("Main Pump Status" = pump 1 high). Same Button codes 0x01/0x02/0x04/0x05/0x12 confirmed. The CC encoding is [K, K ⊕ 0xE0 ⊕ code]. 24 177 CC frames, random K The first Temp press only enters set mode, so the v1 controller was always one press short. d2 bit 5 and d13 0x98 at t≈210 Heating sequence: pump 1 low → d1 bit 5 → heater bit d10.6 t≈454–513 Lights layout (mode, R/G/B, brightness) matched HJ's map. The owner's colour names were the independent check. t≈294–414 Date packing d7 = (day << 3) ⊕ month: explains May, HJ's "January", and November's 0x2B. Months 8–12 can't be separated from the fold alone. D1–D7

docs.title: 4 November 2026: the rebuild
docs.text: Decision Rationale Tub definitions are data (definitions/*.yaml + JSON Schema): message type, field map with transforms and an evidence status, buttons, entities The May 2025 goal, finally without per-tub code. A new Balboa-family tub is a YAML file. A new cipher family is one codec in Python and C++. Layers: transport → protocol → tub (sans-IO bus state machine, setpoint controller) → HA Each layer testable alone. The bus logic is pure, so a mock board can drive it. Transmit off by default; one marked TX choke point; lazy channel claim; command entities unavailable while off; a static test asserts nothing else writes The owner's "never touch the real bus during development" constraint, and a lesson from v1's start-up transmit. Keep HA identities: same device id, bare unique_ids, and discovery published to the exact ha-mqtt-discoverable topics Retained configs are replaced in place: no duplicates, no orphans, no entity renames. Drop ha-mqtt-discoverable for raw paho Needed exact topic control; one fewer heavy dependency. Closed-loop setpoint control (one press in flight, confirm in the next status frames, retry, bounded attempts) Directly serves the running-cost goal: setpoint automations must land reliably. Native ESPHome component reading the same YAML at compile time; a framework-free C++ core tested on the host against the same fixtures No EW11, no cloud, no sidecar. One source of truth for both runtimes. Old implementation on branch legacy/pre-rewrite Rollback until the switch-over.

docs.title: 4 November 2026: per-byte decryption and giving back
docs.text:
Finding Evidence Consequence The fold loses data. With the per-frame key removed, both bytes of some pairs change. D7: bytes 2 and 3, bytes 28 and 29 Decode per byte, not per pair. One key stream decodes everything: pyjacuzzi's formula with four bytes corrected by −8. Wall clock, topside labels, D1 and D7 decode: decrypt in the definition; no per-field XORs. The same stream decodes the Sundance 780 and another encrypted Jacuzzi. HyperActiveJ's sample frame (14 Apr 2022); a pyjacuzzi frame labelled by its author The August–December date gap closes, the fold's year is shown to be wrong on other tubs, and a definition written for one board fits the family. Correction: the fold's weekday was right all along. The "off by one" on foreign frames came from the fold's wrong year. Same frames Docs corrected.

An issue for HyperActiveJ's repository (now pete-jorgensen/SundanceHotTub2MQTT) was drafted. It answers the open question in their DECODING.md §3.8 and includes a standalone decoder, tested on their own sample frame. That is the first thing this project has given back to the work it is built on.

docs.title: 9 November 2026: a second tub, on someone else's evidence
docs.text: Decision Rationale Jacuzzi J345 (plain protocol through a ProLink module): definitions/jacuzzi_j345.yaml, decoded from the contributor's five May 2025 logs (three more recovered from the threads into tests/fixtures/captures/unencrypted/) The tub from the 18 May 2025 "J335" config. Its owner had asked for progress in December 2025. The model name was settled from the owner's own words: J345. A direct bus mode: fixed address 0x0A, no channel claim, one frame per four status frames The ProLink stream has no clear-to-send. pyjacuzzi wrote straight to the socket and it worked. Transmit limited to frames the pyjacuzzi capture shows working, reproduced byte for byte in tests Nobody on the project can test this tub. Home Assistant device name and identifier default from the definition Environment-only installs could not set them, and the second tub would have appeared as "Jacuzzi J235". Bridge only: ESPHome rejects the protocol Nobody has wired an ESP32 to a plain board.

docs.title: Threads worth telling in the write-up
docs.text:
• Pluggability as a slow-burning requirement. README concepts (May 2025) → class-name loading per family (May 2025) → a contributor's J335 config (18 May 2025) → "protocol abstraction" (Apr 2026) → schema-validated data files shared by two runtimes (Nov 2026).
  • Folklore vs evidence. Three generations of magic XOR constants turned out to be one cipher seen through a lossy fold. The decisive tests were mundane: commit dates, filename epochs and the owner typing "p1 press 2" into a terminal.
  • The value of a labelled capture. Eighteen months of guessing about pump bits were settled by nine minutes of receive-only capture with a script of topside actions.
  • Giving back. The labelled capture answered a question that HyperActiveJ had asked in writing, and the fix decodes their own sample frame. Posting it upstream closes the loop.
  • Safety as design. Receive-only by default, one choke point, and a static test. Development never transmitted to the real tub.

docs.title: Monitor and capture
docs.text:
Three tools let you look at the bus without any risk to the tub. None of them can transmit.

  • spa2mqtt monitor decodes the live bus and prints the values to your terminal. Use it to check wiring, check a tub definition, and watch what changes when you press a topside button.
  • spa2mqtt capture prints the bus messages themselves, one per line, and leaves out the repeats. Use it to see what the tub sends, or to share a short log.
  • tools/capture.py records the raw bytes of the bus to a file, with labels that you type. Use it to collect evidence for a new tub definition or a bug report.

All three need a connection to the bus. Most RS485-to-TCP adapters, the EW11A included, accept only one TCP client. Stop the bridge before you run any of them.

docs.title: spa2mqtt monitor
docs.text:
spa2mqtt monitor HOST [options]
spa2mqtt monitor --serial DEVICE [options]
spa2mqtt monitor --replay CAPTURE [options]

In Docker, put the same command after the image name:

docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/srleach/spa2mqtt:2 spa2mqtt monitor 192.168.1.100

docs.title: Why it cannot transmit
docs.text:
The monitor has three separate guards. Each one alone stops a write:

  1. The tub model runs with transmit off, so the bus state machine never produces a frame.
  2. The monitor creates no bus writer, so no code path in it can send.
  3. The connection is wrapped in a read-only transport, whose write method raises an error.

The monitor also never connects to MQTT, so Home Assistant sees nothing.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning HOST Address of the RS485-to-TCP adapter -p, --port PORT 8899 TCP port of the adapter --serial DEVICE Read a USB RS485 adapter, for example /dev/ttyUSB0, instead of TCP. Needs the serial extra --replay CAPTURE Decode a capture file instead of the live bus --speed N 0 Replay speed. 0 is as fast as possible, 1 is real time -d, --definition ID jacuzzi_j235 Tub definition ID or file path -i, --interval SECONDS 10 Seconds between full reports --describe off Show each field's note in the reports --quiet-changes off Print only the periodic reports, not each change --json off Print JSON lines instead of text, for scripts --record FILE Also append the raw bytes to FILE, in the capture format below. --record - writes them to standard output, between the reports

Give exactly one source: HOST, --serial or --replay.

In the container image the working directory is read-only for the unprivileged user. To record, mount a directory and run as your own user:

docker run --rm -it --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD:/captures" \
  ghcr.io/srleach/spa2mqtt:2 spa2mqtt monitor 192.168.1.100 --record /captures/session.log

Where you cannot mount a directory, for example Portainer under Home Assistant OS, use --record -. The capture lines then appear in the container log, mixed with the reports. Copy the log into a file: spa2mqtt replay and spa2mqtt monitor --replay read the capture lines and skip everything else.

docs.title: What it prints
docs.text:
The monitor prints a full report at once, and then one every --interval seconds. A report contains:

  • the latest raw status frame and its decoded payload,
  • every field of the definition, with its value and its evidence status (confirmed, inferred or hypothesis),
  • frame rates per message type,
  • the checksum error count.

Between reports, the monitor prints each value change and each topside button press as it happens. Press Ctrl-C to stop. The monitor prints a last report when it stops.

A rising checksum error count means the bytes are damaged on the way. Check the baud rate (115200, 8N1) and the A and B wires.

docs.title: spa2mqtt capture
docs.text:
capture prints each message (frame) on the bus as one line. A bus repeats itself many times a second, so capture prints a frame only when it differs from the last frame of the same kind. Two frames are the same kind when they have the same address and the same message type.

spa2mqtt capture HOST [options]
spa2mqtt capture --serial DEVICE [options]
spa2mqtt capture --replay FILE [options]

With Docker:

docker run --rm -it ghcr.io/srleach/spa2mqtt:2 spa2mqtt capture 192.168.1.100

Like the monitor, it reads through a wrapper that refuses every write, and it has no writer. Stop it with Ctrl-C.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Meaning HOST Address of the RS485-to-TCP adapter -p, --port 8899 TCP port of the adapter. Use 4257 for a ProLink module -d, --definition jacuzzi_j235 Tub definition. It tells capture which frames carry a key (see below) -o, --output FILE Append the lines to FILE and print nothing --all off Print every frame, repeats too --serial DEVICE Read a USB RS485 adapter instead of TCP. Needs the serial extra --replay FILE Read a capture file instead of the live bus. Use it to shorten a capture you already have --speed N 0 Replay speed. 0 is as fast as possible, 1 is real time

docs.title: What it prints
docs.text:
# spa2mqtt capture: Jacuzzi J235 from 192.168.1.100:8899, started 2026-11-09T20:41:59+0000. Read-only. Repeated frames are left out.
1793830074.160 RX 7e0510bf065c7e  # 0x10 clear to send
1793830074.160 RX 7e0710bfcc59b9177e  # 0x10 panel/button
1793830074.160 RX 7e26ffafc40b190f…497e  # 0xFF status
1793830166.368 RX 7e0710bfcc7f9b617e  # 0x10 panel/button, after 4127 repeats
# 51242 frames: 434 shown, 50808 repeats left out, 0 crc errors, 0 resyncs

Each line has the time, the frame as hex, and a note after #. The note gives the address, the message type, and how many repeats of that kind were left out since the line before it. The last line counts the frames when you stop.

The J235 sends every status, lights and panel frame with a new random key, so the bytes differ even when nothing changed. capture removes the key before it compares those frames. A frame is printed only when its content changed. The line still shows the bytes exactly as they were received.

In the nine-minute J235 fixture, 51 242 frames become 434 lines.

The output is in the capture file format. The notes are comments, so the file plays back with spa2mqtt replay and spa2mqtt monitor --replay, and it decodes to the same state changes as the full capture. It does not keep the timing between repeated frames. For a new tub definition or a timing question, record everything with tools/capture.py or spa2mqtt monitor --record.

docs.title: tools/capture.py
docs.text:
capture.py records raw bus traffic from an RS485-to-TCP adapter. It has no send call at all. The labels that you type go to the log file only.

git clone https://github.com/srleach/spa2mqtt.git && cd spa2mqtt
python3 tools/capture.py 192.168.1.100 8899

The tool needs only the Python standard library. It writes spa-capture-<time>.log in the current folder.

While it runs, type a short label and press Enter just before each action at the topside, for example pump 1 press or set 38.5 to 39.0. Labels mark the moment in the file, so you can match each change in the bytes to what you did. Press Ctrl-C to stop.

docs.title: File format
docs.text:
Each line is one record:

<unix time> RX <hex bytes exactly as received>
<unix time> MARK <label>

Text after # is a comment. spa2mqtt monitor --record FILE and spa2mqtt capture write the same format. Captures in this format play back with spa2mqtt replay FILE and with spa2mqtt monitor --replay FILE.

docs.title: A good capture
docs.text:
1. Start the capture with the tub idle. Let it run for about one minute.
  2. Note the topside display: water temperature, setpoint and clock. Type them as a label.
  3. Do one action at a time. Type a label first, do the action, then wait about ten seconds.
  4. Cover each button: each pump, the light, setpoint up and down.
  5. Stop with Ctrl-C.

docs.title: Contribute a capture
docs.text:
Captures of other tubs, or of a J235 doing something new, help the project. A capture contains only bus bytes, times and your labels. It contains no network addresses or passwords. Read your labels before you share the file.

  1. Open an issue and attach the capture. Name the tub model, the board, and what the labels mean.
  2. Or open a pull request that adds the file to tests/fixtures/captures/raw/. The test suite replays every capture there through the decoder. Add the expected values to tests/test_replay.py if you know them. That folder is for tubs of the encrypted family, because its captures are also decoded with the J235 definition. A capture of another family goes in its own folder under tests/fixtures/captures/.

To decode a capture yourself:

spa2mqtt replay spa-capture-1762466000.log
spa2mqtt monitor --replay spa-capture-1762466000.log --describe

replay prints each state change with its frame number. monitor --replay prints the full reports.

docs.title: Jacuzzi plain protocol (unencrypted boards, via ProLink)
docs.text:
This document describes the protocol of unencrypted Jacuzzi boards as far as one tub shows it: a Jacuzzi J345 (J-300 series) reached through the Jacuzzi ProLink module. It is the reference for definitions/jacuzzi_j345.yaml and for the bridge's direct bus mode. The J235 does not use these frames: see the wire protocol for the encrypted boards.

Ground truth rule. Where sources disagree, the captured dumps win. Statuses mean the same as in the wire protocol, with this tub in place of the J235. Nobody on the project has this tub, so no claim here was checked by the project against the tub itself. The checks are the owner's captures, pyjacuzzi's code, and the tub's recorded reaction to commands that pyjacuzzi sent.

Index convention. p[n] is payload byte n, counted from 0 at the first byte after TYPE. A field's byte: n in the definition uses the same index. pyjacuzzi and jackbrown1993 index the whole frame: their data[k] is p[k-5].

docs.title: Dumps (one J345, this repo)
docs.text:
All five files are in tests/fixtures/captures/unencrypted/. tests/test_plain_j345.py replays them and asserts the values cited below. "S L8 → L9" means: sent on line 8 of S, effect seen on line 9.

docs.title: 1. Framing
docs.text:
The frame is the same as on the encrypted boards (wire protocol §2):

 7E | LEN | ADDR | MID | TYPE | payload ... | CRC | 7E
Claim Status Evidence LEN = total bytes − 2. CRC-8 (poly 0x07, init 0x02, xorout 0x02) over LEN through the last payload byte. Confirmed All 2 133 frames in S, D, X1–X3 decode with the existing decoder: 0 CRC errors, 0 resyncs The payload is plaintext: no per-frame key, no key stream. Confirmed Identical states give identical frames (D L6–L75 repeat one frame); S: a sent 20 5a appears as p[9] = 5a spa2mqtt.protocol needs no change for these frames. Confirmed Frame.encode() reproduces every captured frame, sent and received

Four 7-byte records. Record k is p[7k .. 7k+6]:

Offset Field Status Evidence 0 Mode: 00 off, 01–09 colours, 80 blend, ff blend paused Confirmed (record 0) Every 21 1f MM command gives mode MM in the next frame (§5). 80, ff from the topside: X3 L1354, L1376. PJ L1546 1 Sub-mode: 02, then 04, only in blend Unknown X2 L19; X3 L1354, L1363 2 Brightness, percent Confirmed 21 2f … LL gives LL (S L63 → L64 and following). docs.title: 5. Commands
docs.text:
Every command is sent to ADDR 0x0A, MID 0xBF, in plaintext. These are the complete frames from S. Frame(0x0A, 0xBF, type, payload).encode() reproduces each one, and tests/test_plain_j345.py asserts that the bridge emits exactly these bytes.

Command Frame S line (sent → seen) Tub's reaction Panel request 7e 07 0a bf 19 01 00 95 7e 3 → 4 Reply 7e 07 0a bf 1b 13 0c 1a 7e after 96 ms Set temperature 90 °F 7e 06 0a bf 20 5a 93 7e 8 → 9 p[9] 50 → 5a Set temperature 100 °F 7e 06 0a bf 20 64 29 7e 10 → 11 p[9] → 64; circulation pump starts Set temperature 101 °F 7e 06 0a bf 20 65 2e 7e 13 → 14 p[9] → 65 Button, pump 1 7e 06 0a bf 17 04 9c 7e 22 → 23, 24 → 25 p[10] 02 → 0a → 02 Button, pump 2 7e 06 0a bf 17 05 9b 7e 17 → 18, 20 → 21 p[10] 02 → 22 → 02 Light colour MM 7e 0d 0a bf 21 1f MM 00 00 00 00 ff 00 CRC 7e below All four records show mode MM Light brightness LL 7e 0d 0a bf 21 2f 01 00 00 00 00 LL 00 CRC 7e below Brightness = LL; 00 turns every record off Colour MM CRC Sent on S line Brightness LL CRC Sent on S line 01 white 77 26, 47 00 (off) f9 57, 78 02 blue 11 29, 60 14 (20) fa 63 03 green ce 32 28 (40) ff 66 04 yellow dd 50 3c (60) fc 69 05 orange 02 35 50 (80) f5 72 06 red 64 38 64 (100) 58 75 07 violet bb 41 08 amber 42 54 09 aqua 9d 44

Notes:

  • All 26 sends took effect on the first attempt. The tub reacts within one status period (95–374 ms); light changes show within one lights period.
  • The 01 after 2f is not a mode: the mode stayed 02 (S L64).
  • The ff brightness in a colour command left the brightness at 60. Whether 60 is a default or the previous value is unknown.
  • PJ jacuzziui.py L482–500: the board refuses mode 0 (turn off with brightness 0) and refuses blend (80) as a direct command. PJ L487–499 enters blend by sending brightness 0 and then a non-zero brightness. So a non-zero brightness command sent while the lights are off is expected to start blend mode. In S every non-zero brightness (L63–L75) was sent while the mode was 02, so this is not proven on this tub.
  • PJ jacuzzi.py L394–397 doubles the set-temperature value when the tub is in Celsius (half degrees C in the same byte). No capture shows Celsius mode. The definition's requires: {celsius_mode: false} makes the bridge refuse the 0x20 command unless the last status frame has p[13] bit 0 clear.

Not proven on this tub. spa2mqtt does not send any of these:

  • 0x17 codes 01 temp up, 02 temp down, 11 light, 12 colour, 0f UV, 1e menu (JB jacuzziRS485.py L100–107, another tub).
  • Set time (0x18), locks (0x1F), filter commands (0x1B/0x1C), module-ident request (0x04), 0x1A buttons (PJ only).
  • Any 0x20 value other than 5a, 64, 65. The definition offers 80–104 °F, the lowest and highest setpoints any capture shows (S L5, X3 L1241), with the same one-byte encoding. How the tub treats a value outside its own range is unknown, so the bridge never builds one.

docs.title: 6. Transport: the ProLink module
docs.text:
Claim Status Evidence The ProLink serves the bus as raw frames on TCP port 4257. Confirmed Every log of this tub; PJ ProlinkMessageParsing.txt L846, L919 The ProLink has the fixed bus address 0x0A. Confirmed All 26 sent frames and the 0x1B reply in S; PJ L198–202 The stream carries no clear-to-send and no channel traffic. The ProLink appears to arbitrate the bus itself. Confirmed (absence), Inferred (reason) D, X1–X3: 2 074 frames, all FF AF 16 or FF AF 23. The v1 logger printed every frame of every type A client may write a command at any time, with no wait for a poll. Inferred PJ balboa.py L210 opens a bare socket and sends on user action; S: 26 of 26 sends worked pyjacuzzi sends 0x19 01 00 13 ms after connecting. Confirmed S L2 → L3. Whether later commands depend on it is unknown: no capture has a command without it pyjacuzzi spaces repeated presses 1.0 s apart. Confirmed (source) PJ L703–707. The two closest sends in S are 1.96 s apart The ProLink may sleep while the tub is idle. Hypothesis PJ readme.md items 6–7. The bridge reconnects after 30 s of silence

Corroboration for the missing clear-to-send: the owner reported that JB's project showed temperatures on this tub but could not change anything. JB waits for a clear-to-send on its channel (jacuzziRS485.py L200–205), which this stream never delivers.

What is on the RS485 bus behind the ProLink is unknown. An EW11A or ESP32 wired to this board might see clear-to-send frames and need the channel claim of the encrypted boards. Nobody has tried, so the loader rejects a plain definition with bus.mode: claim.

docs.title: 7. What spa2mqtt sends
docs.text:
The definition selects bus.mode: direct (design §6). With transmit on:

  1. Nothing is sent at start-up or on connect.
  2. A command from Home Assistant is queued (at most 8; more are dropped with a warning). A number outside its range is refused, not clamped. A setpoint is refused unless the last status frame shows Fahrenheit.
  3. On the next status frame, the bridge sends the connection_check frame (0x19) if it has not sent it on this TCP connection. bus.hello in the definition names it; without that key it is never sent.
  4. Four status frames later (about 1.2 s) it sends the queued frame, and so on: one frame per four status frames.
  5. Nothing is retried. A reconnect drops the queue and re-arms the connection check.

Every frame goes through BusWriter.send(), so SPA_TRANSMIT=false blocks all of it.

docs.title: 8. Unknowns
docs.text:
1. Whether the 0x19 connection check is needed before commands work.
  2. Whether the ProLink accepts more than one TCP client, or the official app at the same time.
  3. Whether a direct RS485 tap on this board needs the clear-to-send and channel-claim exchange.
  4. Water temperature (p[7]) and the second sensor (p[16]) against the topside display.
  5. The heater bit (p[11] bit 0) and p[11] bits 1, 2 and 4.
  6. p[5] (08 against 02), and the heat-mode and filter-mode fields PJ places there.
  7. Pump low speed, pump 3, blower, UV.
  8. The tub's handling of setpoints other than 90, 100 and 101 °F, and of out-of-range values.
  9. Celsius mode: p[13] bit 0 and any half-degree encoding.
  10. Light records 1–3, the tail and sub-mode bytes, the 1f/2f selector byte, and why pyjacuzzi's command writes four records while the topside writes one.
  11. Whether a non-zero brightness command sent while the lights are off starts blend mode (PJ jacuzziui.py L487–499 says so).
  12. The 0x1B reply 13 0c. PJ reads it as filter start hour 19 and duration 12 h. The hour equals the tub's clock hour at that moment, which may be a coincidence.
  13. p[8] (fa), p[17..18] (01 1c), p[21..24] (80 00 80 00), p[28..31] beyond "0 normal, 1 setpoint edit", and the CLEARRAY counter's fall from 364 to 0 in six days.
  14. Month and year: seen for May 2025 only.

docs.title: Jacuzzi "encrypted" RS485 protocol (J235 and Sundance-family boards)
docs.text:
This document describes the RS485 bus protocol spoken by the Jacuzzi J235 control board (the "encrypted", Sundance-style variant of the Balboa protocol) as far as it is currently understood. It is the reference for spa2mqtt and the spa_bus ESPHome component.

Ground truth rule. Where sources disagree, the captured dumps win. Every claim carries a citation and a status:

Status Meaning Confirmed Verified against J235 dumps with an independent check (wall clock, physical plausibility, CRC, or two independent sources plus a dump). Inferred Consistent with all J235 dumps and at least one source, but no independent check yet. Hypothesis Claimed by a source or suggested by data, never observed exercising on a J235. Unknown No credible interpretation.

Every dump-derived number below can be reproduced with python3 tools/research/analyze_captures.py <section> (cited as [A:section]).

docs.title: 1. Physical layer
docs.text: Claim Status Evidence Two-wire RS485, half duplex, shared by the board, topside panel(s) and add-on modules. Confirmed Legacy README wiring "12v +/, A/B" (S2M README.md); bus has several channels (§4). 115200 baud, 8N1. Inferred IR README.md L197 ("115200 8N1, required by the bus", Sundance). The J235 has been read through an EW11A RS485–WiFi bridge (port 8899, S2M config.yml.example); its serial settings are not recorded in this repo. Confirm from the EW11A web UI. An EW11A in transparent TCP mode passes bytes unmodified (no escaping). Confirmed D1 and D7: 51 296 frames, 0 CRC errors, 0 resyncs [A:crc]. Devices on the J235 bus: the board, one topside panel on channel 0x10, the (passive) EW11A. Confirmed D7 census: only 0x10 is ever polled and it answers every CTS [A:census].

docs.title: 2. Framing
docs.text:
0     1     2      3     4      5 .. N-3     N-2   N-1
 7E | LEN | ADDR | MID | TYPE | payload ... | CRC | 7E
Claim Status Evidence Start and end flag 0x7E. Confirmed D1: all 54 frames [A:crc]; SC L242/L250; PJ src/balboa.py L10. LEN counts from LEN through CRC: LEN = total_frame_bytes − 2. Confirmed D1 [A:crc] "LEN==len(frame)-2: True"; PJ docs/ProlinkMessageParsing.txt L4. No byte stuffing or escaping. A 0x7E inside the payload is legal; the receiver must frame by LEN, not by scanning for 0x7E. Confirmed (no escaping), Inferred (0x7E payload bytes) PJ balboa.py L777–821 frames by length; D1 bodies are uniformly random per frame (key byte, §3.1), so payload 0x7E is unavoidable. Legacy S2M resynchronised on 7E <non-7E>, which is correct. CRC-8 over bytes [1 .. N−3] (LEN through last payload byte). Confirmed D1 54/54 [A:crc]; SC balboa_calc_cs(data[1:len]) L249. CRC parameters: poly 0x07, init 0x02, no reflection, xorout 0x02 (textbook form). The legacy "augmented, register 0xB5" code is the same function. Confirmed [A:crc] "formulations agree=True"; garbled1 docstring in S2M spas/base/packet/packet.py L631–650. AL's "init 0xFF / xorout 0xFF" variant gives identical results (0x02⊕0xFF is a fixed point), per the upstream review. Observed lengths: C4 LEN=0x26 (33-byte payload), CA LEN=0x22 (29-byte payload), CC LEN=0x07 (2-byte payload), CTS 0x06 and new-client 0x00 LEN=0x05 (empty payload). Confirmed D7 census [A:census]. Consecutive frames each carry their own start and end flag (… 7E 7E …). Confirmed D7 raw stream. Receivers should reject LEN < 5 or LEN > 64. Inferred (design choice) IR accepts 5–64; S2M legacy accepted ≤128; the longest known frame is 0x26.
