Note SC/HJ/JB build this frame with an off-by-one (bytearray(9) then write index 9), so this path has probably never run successfully. 0x06 channel 0xBF board → client Clear to send for that channel, ≈ 45 Hz to 0x10 Confirmed D7: each CTS is followed by the panel's CC [A:census]; SC L731–748. 0x07 channel 0xBF client → board Nothing to send Hypothesis SC L23, L642–648 (built, never sent: L743 commented out). 0x16 / 0x17 / 0x23 Unencrypted Jacuzzi status / button / lights. Not used by the J235. Documented for the J345 in Wire protocol (plain boards). Confirmed (not J235) No such frames in D1; PJ L1617–1665 and HJ DECODING.md L275–303 treat these as plaintext on non-encrypted boards. The legacy S2M and SC route 0x16/0x23 through the XOR decoder, which is wrong (HJ upstream removed it for that reason).

The address and MID semantics follow the Balboa convention: MID=0xAF is a board broadcast, 0xBF is client traffic, ADDR=0xFE is "unassigned client" and 0xFF is broadcast (Inferred: SC constants; PJ docs/ProlinkMessageTypes.txt L28). The Prolink module uses fixed ADDR=0x0A (PJ L198–202). Sundance/J-series panels have been seen on 0x10 and 0x11 (SC L238 example; HJ DECODING.md L366).

docs.title: 3.2 Encryption of C4 (status)
docs.text:
Superseded for decoding by §3.3. This section explains the two published models and how they relate. spa2mqtt 2.0 decoded with the pairwise fold. The current decode removes the key and a calibrated key stream and reads plaintext per byte (§3.3).

Two published models exist. They are algebraically the same cipher. This repo proves it on D1. The first version of this document chose the pairwise fold because it is key-independent and because it gave the right calendar day where pyjacuzzi's per-byte layout did not.

Per-frame key byte. payload[0] (frame byte 5) is a random per-frame key K. Every other payload byte is K ⊕ c_i for a fixed per-state stream c. In D1, 49 distinct keys appear across 54 frames, but payload ⊕ K is identical for every frame in the same tub state [A:cipher]. (Confirmed.)

Model A: key-stream decrypt (PJ src/jacuzzi.py L221–292):

key1 = f[5] ^ 0x19            # 0x59 for CA, 0xDF for CC
key2 = LEN - 7
for i in 6 .. LEN-1:          # frame indices; CRC untouched
    key2 = (key2 - 1) mod 64
    P[i] = f[i] ^ key1 ^ key2

Model B: pairwise fold (HyperActiveJ xormsg, SC L262–267; legacy S2M):

d[j] = payload[2j] ^ payload[2j+1] ^ 1        for j = 0..15   (payload[32] is never used)

Identity (Confirmed on all 54 D1 frames [A:cipher]; independently derived in the upstream review): d[0] = P[6] ^ 0x06 and d[j] = P[5+2j] ^ P[6+2j] for j ≥ 1. Consequences:

  • HJ's "hour XOR 6" is the key-stream constant. Model A's hour P[6] equals d[0] ^ 6.
  • Model B values are XORs of two adjacent Model A bytes. HJ's "temperature XOR 2" is really P[15] ^ P[16] with P[16] = 0x02 in every sample (D1; PJ samples). PJ's "minute (P[27]&0x3F)^0x08 for some unknown reason" is P[27] ^ P[28] with P[28] = 0x08.
  • Which model gives the true field boundaries is not settled. The evidence favours Model B: D1 was committed 2025-05-16 at 16:49 +0100, and its hour/minute read 11:35–11:38. Model B gives day-of-month 16, month 5. Model A gives P[19]>>3 = 19, three days in the future. Model B's day/month also matches wall clock on four further dates (D2–D6, §5). (Day field: Confirmed for Model B; refuted for Model A on J235.)
  • Model B discards half the information (16 of 32 bytes). Fields that are not 1:1 with a folded byte may be invisible to it. This is the main reason raw captures are needed (§9).

Encoding (for transmit, §6): to send a folded payload d, pick any K and emit payload[0]=K, payload[2j+1]=payload[2j]^d[j]^1. Model B decoding is insensitive to the choice of the even bytes, but the board decodes with whatever it really uses, so outbound C4 encoding is never needed and is not implemented.

docs.title: 3.3 Decryption: plaintext per byte (current decode)
docs.text:
Method. Remove the per-frame key, then remove a fixed key stream:

plain[i] = payload[i] ^ payload[0] ^ S[i]          (i = 1 .. 32; plain[0] = 0)
S[i]     = 0x19 ^ ((31 - i + adjust[i]) mod 64)     adjust[i] = -8 at i = 5, 6, 14, 15, 22; else 0

Every field is then a plain read of one byte (or some of its bits), with no per-field constant. S is pyjacuzzi's key stream (decrypt(), key1 = payload[0] ^ 0x19, key2 counting down from 31) with five corrections. [A:decrypt] prints the table.

Why per byte. After the key is removed, varying data shows up in both bytes of some pairs (D7: bytes 2 and 3, bytes 28 and 29). The fold merges each pair into one value, so it loses information whenever both bytes change. This is what made the date undecodable from August to December (§5 d7) and what made the "secondary temperature" and the display code look multiplexed.

How the stream was established.

Byte Field Evidence for S[i] on the bits used pyjacuzzi formula 1 hour Wall clock D3–D6; pyjacuzzi labelled frame (2:40 PM) correct 2 pump 1 running (bit 6), heat demand (bit 5), manual circ (bit 7) D7 presses correct on bits 5–7 3 pump 2 (bit 2) D7 presses correct on bit 2 5 day of week (bits 2–0), pump 1 speed (4–3), set mode (5) Five dated J235 captures; D7 presses 8 lower 6 filter change days D8 topside FC 172 (the formula gives 164); D7 177 five days earlier 8 lower 10 water temperature D7 display 38.5 °C; pyjacuzzi label 102 °F correct 14 day of month (bits 7–3) D1 16 May, D7 4 Nov; pyjacuzzi label 18 May 8 lower 15 month (bits 3–0) D1 May, D7 November; pyjacuzzi label May 8 lower 16 setpoint D7 38.5 → 40.0 → 38.5; pyjacuzzi label 103 °F correct 19 year − 2000 2025, 2026 (J235); pyjacuzzi label 2023 correct 21 heater (bit 6) D7 heating sequence correct on bit 6 22 minute Wall clock D3–D6; pyjacuzzi label 2:40 PM 8 lower 24 water change days D8 topside H2O 150 correct 27 UV lamp days D8 topside UV 148 correct

Status: Confirmed on the bits listed, for the J235. Bytes not listed use the formula without correction and are unverified. pyjacuzzi's own "minute (b & 0x3F) ^ 0x08 for some unknown reason" is the byte-22 correction.

Cross-check on other tubs. The same stream, calibrated only on the J235, decodes every raw C4 frame published by other projects [A:decrypt], tests/test_replay.py:

Frame Plaintext Check HyperActiveJ Sundance 780 docstring sample (fc38ab5) 14:17 Thu 14/04/2022, water 96 °F, set 90 °F Thursday is right for that date; HyperActiveJ's first commits are 15–16 Apr 2022 pyjacuzzi jacuzzi.py L1124, labelled "05/18/23 2:40PM, WS 103, WT 102" 14:40 Thu 18/05/2023, water 102, set 103 Every labelled value matches pyjacuzzi jacuzzi.py L246 13:37 Tue 09/05/2023, water 96, set 97 Valid date and weekday

The fold reads the year of the first two as 2023 and 2022, both wrong. Status: the cipher and stream are Confirmed to be shared by the J235, another encrypted Jacuzzi and the Sundance 780.

Agreement with the fold. On all 1 858 raw J235 frames, the plaintext fields equal the old fold result wherever the fold was right (test_per_byte_agrees_with_fold_on_every_raw_frame). The differences are the corrections: the November day of month, and two pump-start frames in which the fold mixed the pump flag into the secondary value.

docs.title: 3.4 Encryption of CC (button command)
docs.text:
payload = [K, K ^ 0xE0 ^ code], i.e. button code = payload[0] ^ payload[1] ^ 0xE0. (Confirmed: in D7 the panel's 24 177 CC frames use a random K every time, and every labelled press decodes to the expected code [A:labelled].)

  • HJ sends [0xE0|code, 0x00] (SC L245–248: data[5]=val, data[6]=0, with val 225 etc.).
  • PJ sends key 0x00 then Model A with key1 0xDF on a 1-byte body, which gives [0x00, code ^ 0xDF ^ 0x3F] = [0x00, code ^ 0xE0] (PJ L294–346).
  • SC's idle-panel example 7E 07 10 BF CC 65 85 A6 7E decodes to code 0x00 ("no button") (0x65^0x85^0xE0 = 0).
  • HJ's observed panel frames decode to P2 (0xE5) and P1 (0xE4) under this rule (HJ DECODING.md L366–369, per the upstream review).

Plain codes are shared with the unencrypted Jacuzzi 0x17/0x1A commands:

Code HJ value (0xE0|code) Function Status 0x00 224 none / idle (sent by the panel on every CTS) Confirmed (D7) 0x01 225 Temp up. The first press only enters set mode; later presses step +0.5 °C Confirmed (D7 t≈210, 238–239, 454) 0x02 226 Temp down (same set-mode behaviour) Confirmed (D7 t≈272–273, 482–484) 0x04 228 Pump 1: off → low → high → off Confirmed (D7 t≈90, 119, 143) 0x05 229 Pump 2: off ↔ on Confirmed (D7 t≈181, 196) 0x12 242 Light: each press steps off → blend → colours → off (§3.5) Confirmed (D7 t≈294–414) 0x0F 239 ClearRay (UV) / circulation Hypothesis (HJ, JB). PJ docs say 0x0E (internally inconsistent). Not on the J235 topside. 0x11 241 Light on/off Hypothesis. The J235 panel never sent it; its single light button is 0x12. 0x1E 254 Menu Hypothesis (defined in HJ, never sent; HJ warns against brute-forcing codes)

The J235 has no direct "set temperature" command on the encrypted bus. Setpoint changes are made by pressing Temp up/down and watching the reported setpoint (§7). (Inferred: SC L209, L259, L405–415; PJ L399–458 "no command to set an arbitrary value".)

docs.title: 3.5 Lights (CA)
docs.text:
The CA payload (29 bytes) folds to 14 bytes c0..c13. HJ's assignment is confirmed by D7, with the owner's colour labels as the independent check [A:labelled]:

c Meaning Status Evidence (D7) 0 constant 0xBD Unknown – 1 brightness / on: 0x64 (100) on, 0 off Confirmed t≈294 on, 307 off 2 blue level Confirmed "blue" → c2=FF; "cyan" → c2=c6=7F; "white" → c2=c6=c8=55 3, 5 constants 0x64, 0xFF Unknown – 4 mode: 0x80 blend, 0xFF transition, 0x01 white, 0x02 blue, 0x03 green, 0x06 red, 0x07 violet, 0x08 amber ("green" to the owner), 0x09 aqua Confirmed press sequence t≈294–414; matches HJ DECODING.md map 6 green level Confirmed "deep green" → c6=FF 8 red level Confirmed "red" → c8=FF; "magenta" → c2=c8=7F 9 0x02 while blending, 0x04 at step, 0 static Inferred (blend phase/speed) – 7, 10–13 0 Unknown –

Blend mode animates c2/c6/c8 about once a second.

Light button timing (Confirmed, D7 t≈294–516 [A:labelled]). A 0x12 press steps to the next mode only while it follows the previous light press closely: presses 0.6–3.5 s apart stepped blend → blend paused → blue → violet → red → amber → green → aqua → white. A press 5.2 s or more after the last one turned the light off (t≈306.1, 323.9, 340.6, 357.3, 373.4, 393.6, 408.6), and a press while off turned it on in blend. The owner's label at t≈442: "light changes in steps only for few secs then toggles off". The J235 definition reads c1 bit 6 as Light (on/off) and c4 as Light Mode; the Light switch waits ≈ 7.5 s between presses so that a press which only stepped the colour is followed by one that turns the light off.

docs.title: 4. Bus arbitration and addressing (state machine)
docs.text:
The board polls every client channel with CTS (0x06). A client may transmit only in the gap immediately after the CTS addressed to its channel. Panels answer every CTS with a CC (code 0x00 when idle). (Inferred: SC L731–770; IR.)

                 (passive listener: never transmits)
 LISTEN ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ observe CTS(0x06) channels  → known_channels                       │
   │ observe CC(0xCC) channels   → active_channels                      │
   ▼ a command is queued AND transmit is enabled                        │
 CLAIM ── after ≥5 CC frames observed: pick lowest channel in           │
   │      known_channels \ active_channels ("dormant") ──► READY        │
   │      none dormant: on next 0x00 send 0x01 request (F1 73)          │
   ▼                                                                     │
 REQUESTED ── 0x02 response: channel = payload[0]; send 0x03 ack ──► READY
 READY ── on CTS(our channel): send one queued CC, else nothing         │
   │      on CC from another device on our channel → conflict ─────────┘ (back to LISTEN)
Claim Status Evidence "Dormant channel" reuse: after 5 CC observations, take the lowest polled channel that never sends CC. Hypothesis; not applicable to this J235 install SC L46–48, L749–760; IR uses 5 CTS frames. D7: the only polled channel (0x10) answers every CTS, so there is no dormant channel and a new client must use the 0x00/0x01 request. Channel request 7E 08 FE BF 01 02 F1 73 cs 7E sent in response to 0x00. Hypothesis SC L687–701. After CTS the client should answer immediately; no deadline is documented. HJ over TCP (EW11A) worked, so the window is at least tens of ms. Inferred SC L742–748; HJ sets TCP_NODELAY (SC L193). IR waits 50 µs for DE/RE turnaround. An idle client may stay silent on CTS. HJ never sends NTS (0x07). Inferred SC L743 commented out. The legacy S2M bridge claims a channel and may send 0x01/0x03 automatically at start-up, even if no button is pressed. Confirmed (code) S2M spas/jacuzzi_encrypted/spa/jacuzzi_encrypted_spa.py L51–88, L1182–1188. The rewrite does not do this (design.md §Safety).

docs.title: 5. C4 status field map (J235)
docs.text:
Index = folded byte d[j] (Model B). The equivalent Model A bytes are P[5+2j] and P[6+2j]. "Bit n" counts from LSB 0. Scale 0.5 assumes °C, the only mode ever observed on this tub (§8). "D7 t≈N" refers to seconds into the labelled capture, printed by [A:labelled].

d Field Transform Status Evidence 0 Hour (24 h) d0 ^ 0x06 Confirmed [A:clock]: D3 13:01 vs wall 12:58Z; D4 13:12 vs 13:09Z; D5 13:11 vs 13:08Z; D6 13:13 vs 13:10Z. D2 runs 17:46→21:31 monotonically. In D7 the tub clock reads 21:31 at 22:07 UTC, so it has drifted since May, but hour and minute roll over consistently. 1 bit 7: manual circulation call (d1>>7)&1 Hypothesis SC L341 MANUAL_CIRC = 7. Never set in any J235 dump, D7 included. 1 bit 6: pump 1 running (any speed) (d1>>6)&1 Confirmed D7: set ≈ 0.5 s after the pump-1 press that starts low speed (t≈90.8), stays set through high, clears on off (t≈143.8). Also set when heating starts pump 1 low (t≈454.5). On the J235, pump 1 low is the circulation/heating mode (PJ jacuzzi.py L925–936: "J-235 has no circ pump"). This is what the legacy "Circulation Pump Status" entity has always shown. 1 bit 5: heat demand / flow proven? (d1>>5)&1 Inferred (sequence), meaning Hypothesis D7: in the heating sequence, pump 1 low starts at t≈454.5, d1 bit 5 at t≈496.1, heater bit at t≈512.8. D2 rows 1–277 (heating) also show it. Never set when pumps are run manually. 1 bit 2: pump 2 on (d1>>2)&1 Confirmed D7: set by the pump-2 press at t≈181.2, cleared by the next at t≈195.6. Single speed. SC L339/L355. 2 bits 2–0: day of week (0 = Sunday) d2 & 7 Confirmed [A:clock]: 18 May 2025 (Sun) 0, 19 May (Mon) 1, 20 May (Tue) 2, 16 May (Fri) 5; D7 4 Nov 2026 (Wed) 3. Also right on the three foreign frames (§3.3). An earlier version of this document said the foreign frames disagreed by one day; that came from pairing them with the fold's wrong year. 2 bits 4–3: pump 1 speed (0 off, 1 low, 2 high) (d2>>3) & 3 Confirmed D7: press 1 → 0x03→0x0B (low), press 2 → 0x13 (high), press 3 → 0x03 (off) at t≈90/119/143. Heating starts low (t≈454.5); D2's heating window has bit 3 set. The legacy "main pump" bit (d2 bit 4) is therefore "pump 1 on high". 2 bit 5: set mode active (topside temperature edit) (d2>>5)&1 Confirmed D7: set by the first temp press and cleared ≈ 5 s after the last (t≈209.9–215.2, 238.2–244.5, 454.5–458.1). docs.title: 6. Commands (transmit path)
docs.text: Claim Status Evidence Frame: 7E 07 <chan> BF CC <K> <K^0xE0^code> <crc> 7E. Inferred §3.4. One frame = one press. Pump buttons cycle off → low → high → off (2-speed pump 1) or off → on → off. Inferred PJ L663–700 (plain boards); legacy S2M exposes raw "pump button" presses for this reason. Send only in the CTS slot for the client's own channel. Inferred §4. There is no acknowledgement. Success is observed only through the next status frames. HJ retries after 2 status frames without change; IR retries after 5, up to 8 attempts. Inferred SC L50, L405–430 CHECKS_BEFORE_RETRY = 2; IR sundance_spa.h.

docs.title: 7. Timing
docs.text: Claim Status Evidence C4 status is broadcast ≈ 3.3 times per second (≈ 300 ms). Confirmed D7: 1 804 C4 in 541 s; D2: 200 rows per full minute. CA lights ≈ 1 Hz; new-client 0x00 ≈ 1 Hz; CTS to 0x10 ≈ 45 Hz, each answered by a CC. Confirmed D7 [A:census]. A topside press is reflected in the next C4 frame (≤ 300 ms). Confirmed D7: CC and the C4 change share a capture chunk timestamp, e.g. t≈239.3 [A:labelled]. Set mode (after the first temp press) times out ≈ 5 s after the last press. Confirmed D7: 5 of 6 periods end 5.2–5.5 s after the last press [A:setmode]. One period ended early, 3.6 s after the last press, in the same frame that pump 1 started for heating. Hypothesis: heat-call start closes the set screen D7 t≈454.5–458.1 [A:setmode]; one occurrence only. C4 repeats unchanged between state changes; consumers must de-duplicate. Confirmed D2 runs of up to 2 313 identical rows [A:timeline]. No status for > 10 s means the link is down (Prolink rule). Inferred PJ docs/ProlinkMessageParsing.txt L1439–1453. The setpoint loop should allow ≥ 2 status frames (≈ 0.6 s) between presses and give up after a bounded number of attempts. Inferred (design) HJ/IR retry constants; PJ waits 1 s between presses. Topside behaviour: the first Temp up/down press only enters set mode; each further press within ≈ 5 s changes the setpoint by 0.5 °C. Confirmed D7 t≈210 (enter only), 238–239 (enter + step), 454 (enter + 2 steps). The legacy (target − current)/0.5 press count was always one short.

docs.title: 7a. Set mode: where it is visible, and how it was validated
docs.text:
Set mode is the topside state entered by the first Temp up/down press, in which further presses step the setpoint. It is visible only in the C4 status broadcast. Every check below comes from D7 [A:setmode].

Check Result Status Two independent indicators d2 bit 5 and d13 (0x98 instead of 0x99) agree on all 1 804 status frames: 119 in set mode, 1 685 not. They come from different byte pairs on the wire. Confirmed Cause All 6 periods start in the same capture chunk as a Temp up/down CC from the topside. No temp press falls outside a period. The setpoint never changes outside a period. Confirmed First press only enters set mode In every period, setpoint steps = presses − 1 (1→0, 2→1, 2→1, 3→2, 2→1, 4→3). Confirmed Timeout 5 of 6 periods end 5.2–5.5 s after the last press. The sixth ends after 3.6 s (§7). Confirmed (≈ 5 s) Other message types CA lights frames continue unchanged. The topside's CC frames carry only the presses, then code 0x00. The 0x00 new-client poll continues. No new address or message type appears. Confirmed Bus cadence 13.40 CTS polls per status frame both inside and outside set mode. (Per-second rates differ by ~5 %, an artefact of per-chunk capture timestamps.) Confirmed

The broadcast placement suggests that the board drives every panel's display from C4, so a second topside would flash the same set screen. That is a hypothesis: no install with two panels has been captured.

Consequence for control. SetpointController reads the set-mode field named by the definition (control.set_mode_field). A press that turns set mode on is the "wake" press, and the next press follows on the next status frame. Without the field, the controller falls back to waiting confirm_frames and retrying. Both paths also wait while the press is still queued for a bus slot. Without that wait, a slow channel grant made the fallback queue duplicate presses and overshoot (regression test test_slow_channel_grant_does_not_duplicate_presses).

docs.title: 8. Units
docs.text: The J235 in D1–D6 reports in °C ×2. Every value is consistent with that: setpoint 76 → 38.0 °C, water 37.5–38.5 °C. (Confirmed for this tub.) No known field on encrypted boards gives the unit flag: PJ upstream 39c2834 explicitly leaves it undetermined for C4. Unit is therefore a configuration value in the tub definition, not a decoded field.

docs.title: 9. Known / inferred / unknown summary
docs.text:
Area Known (Confirmed) Inferred Unknown / Hypothesis Framing 0x7E flags, LEN semantics, CRC-8 (0x07/0x02/0x02), no escaping, own flags per frame Valid LEN range 5–64 – Cipher Per-frame key byte; fold ⇔ key-stream identity; key stream with four corrections (§3.3), shared with the Sundance 780 and another encrypted Jacuzzi; CC [K, K^0xE0^code] – Key stream at bytes not yet tied to a known field Status C4 Hour, minute, day of week, day, month, year, water temp, setpoint, heater, pump 1 running + speed, pump 2, set mode, set screen, cadence, filter / water / UV countdowns (bytes 6, 24, 27) heat-demand sequence; pump-1 flag in byte 29 Manual circ; d10.7; d4, d6; heat mode and filter cycle settings; secondary value byte 28 Lights CA brightness, mode codes, R/G/B positions, ≈ 1 Hz c9 blend phase c0, c3, c5, c7, c10–13 Commands 0x00 idle, 0x01/0x02 temp, 0x04 pump 1, 0x05 pump 2, 0x12 light; press semantics; set-mode first press – ClearRay 0x0F, 0x11, menu 0x1E on J235 Bus Channel 0x10 = topside; CTS ≈ 45 Hz, CC on every CTS; 0x00 ≈ 1 Hz; C4 ≈ 3.3 Hz; the board grants a client channel (0x11 to the bridge, D8) CTS-slot rule The bytes of the request/ack exchange on J235 (not captured); CTS deadline; 0x04/0x05 semantics Physical EW11A transparent bridging 115200 8N1 –

Still open after D8: the filter cycle settings and heat mode (need a capture while they are changed at the topside), manual circulation and the bytes of the J235 channel-request exchange. The bridge's claim works (D8: the board polls 0x11, the bridge's channel, as often as the topside's 0x10), but no capture holds the request and the answer. The FC, H2O and UV countdowns are resolved (bytes 6, 24, 27). In the fold (§5) they sit in d3, d12 and d13: SC's names for d3 and d12 ("water life", "filter life") are swapped, and the "display state" in d13 is mostly the UV countdown. A capture taken while the bridge claims a channel would record the exchange. tools/capture.py produces the capture format; drop files into tests/fixtures/captures/raw/ and the replay tests pick them up.

docs.title: Releases and versions
docs.text:
spa2mqtt uses semantic versioning (semver). A version has three numbers, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH:

  • MAJOR goes up for a breaking change. You may need to change your setup when you upgrade.
  • MINOR goes up for a new feature that does not break anything.
  • PATCH goes up for a fix or any other change.

The first release is v2.0.0. Version 1 was the earlier implementation, kept on the legacy/pre-rewrite branch.

docs.title: How a release happens
docs.text:
Every merge to the main branch makes a release automatically. You do not need to tag by hand, and every change on main gets a version that you can pin. A maintainer can still push a vX.Y.Z tag by hand. The workflow then publishes that tag and creates no new one.

flowchart LR
    A[Pull request merged to main] --> B[Read commits since the last tag]
    B --> C[Compute next version]
    C --> D[Create tag vX.Y.Z]
    D --> E[GitHub release]
    D --> F[Build multi-arch image<br/>push to ghcr.io]

The release workflow reads the commit messages since the newest vX.Y.Z tag. It uses the Conventional Commits style to choose the bump:

Commit message Bump Example type!: or type(scope)!:, or a body line that starts with BREAKING CHANGE Major feat!: rename the transmit setting feat: or feat(scope): Minor feat(esphome): add a light entity Anything else (fix:, docs:, chore:, no type) Patch fix: reconnect after adapter reboot

The largest bump in the range wins. For example, one feat: and three fix: commits give a minor release.

To merge without a release, put [skip release] in the pull request title, or in the message of the commit that lands on main. Use this for changes that do not affect users, for example a CI tweak. The next release then includes those commits.

docs.title: Where releases appear
docs.text:
• Tags: vX.Y.Z in the repository.
  • GitHub releases: github.com/srleach/spa2mqtt/releases, with release notes.
  • Container images: ghcr.io/srleach/spa2mqtt.

docs.title: Image tags
docs.text:
Each release pushes one image, built for linux/amd64, linux/arm64 and linux/arm/v7, under several tags. For release 2.3.1:

Tag Moves to Use it when 2.3.1 Never moves You want exactly this build. Best for rollback 2.3 Each new 2.3.x patch You want fixes only 2 Each new 2.x.y release You want fixes and features, without breaking changes. The default in the deploy files latest Each new release, majors included Not recommended for a tub. A major release can need changes sha-<short> Never moves You need the image for one exact commit

To change the tag, set SPA2MQTT_TAG in .env (Docker Compose) or in the stack's environment variables (Portainer). See Docker Compose and Portainer.

docs.title: Pin ESPHome to a release
docs.text:
ESPHome downloads the component and the entity package from GitHub at compile time. Pin both to the same release tag, so a later change on main cannot change your device the next time you compile:

external_components:
  - source: github://srleach/spa2mqtt@v2.0.0
    components: [spa_bus]

packages:
  spa_entities: github://srleach/spa2mqtt/esphome/packages/jacuzzi_j235.yaml@v2.0.0

Use a full vX.Y.Z tag. ESPHome resolves a git reference, and only full version tags exist. To upgrade, change both tags, then compile and install again. See Build and flash.

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
This site is built with MkDocs Material. The workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml does two jobs:

  • On every pull request, it builds the site with mkdocs build --strict. A broken internal link or a missing page fails the check.
  • On every push to main, it builds the site again and publishes it to the gh-pages branch.

The site appears at https://seanrleach.co.uk/spa2mqtt/ once GitHub Pages is on. The repository owner enables it once:

  1. Open the repository on GitHub and select Settings > Pages.
  2. Under Build and deployment, set Source to Deploy from a branch.
  3. Set Branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root), then select Save.

The gh-pages branch exists after the first push to main that runs the docs workflow. GitHub Pages on a private repository needs a paid plan, so the site may only work after the repository is public.

docs.title: Container image visibility
docs.text:
GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) makes a new package private when the first image is pushed. A private package needs a login to pull, so docker pull fails for other users. After the repository is public, the owner makes the package public once:

  1. Open the repository on GitHub and select the spa2mqtt package under Packages.
  2. Select Package settings.
  3. Under Danger Zone, select Change visibility, then Public.

To preview the site on your computer:

python3 -m venv .venv-docs && . .venv-docs/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/. The page reloads when you save a file.

docs.title: Conflicts and resolutions
docs.text: # Conflict Resolution Evidence 1 Cipher model. HJ folds pairs (b[2j]^b[2j+1]^1) with ad-hoc XORs; PJ uses key byte plus a mod-64 key stream. Proven algebraically identical. HJ fields are XORs of adjacent PJ bytes. The fold is the canonical decode: it is key-independent, and on J235 it gives the correct calendar day while PJ's per-byte day does not. analyze_captures.py cipher; protocol.md §3.2 2 Water temperature XOR. Legacy definition: xor 0x02. PR 17/19: no XOR. XOR 0x02 kept. Without it the D2 heating curve jumps 2.5 °C in 10 min, and heating would stop 1 °C above the setpoint. D2 rows 1–277 3 Byte d10. Legacy debug map: heater bit 6. PR 17: "pump status 0/64/128/192". Bit 6 = heater (set only below setpoint). Bit 7 = unknown, probably auto circulation (HJ upstream). D2 timeline 4 Byte d14. PR 17: hour. SC README: bit 0 = °C flag. HJ: secondary temperature. Hour and °C flag refuted. Secondary temperature kept as a hypothesis. D2: values 22–27 at 20–21 h; bit 0 toggles without a unit change 5 Circulation bit. SC: d1 bit 6. HJ upstream: d4 bit 6. d1 bit 6 for J235 (d4 is constant 0x05 on J235 even while circulating). D2 6 Month. HJ upstream: f7&7 "cannot be right" (read 1 in August). Resolved: d7 = (day << 3) XOR month (4-bit month). It fits May (D1–D6), HJ's "January 19" and D7's 4 November (0x2B). For months 8–12, day bit 0 and month bit 3 collide in the fold, so the fold alone cannot decode dates then. HJ DECODING.md §3.3; D2–D7 7 Day of week. PJ: Model A P[20] & 7 ("not sure"). Plaintext byte 5 bits 2–0 (Sunday = 0), equal to folded d2 & 7. Right on five dated J235 captures and on all three foreign frames. (An earlier version said the foreign frames were off by one; that was the fold's wrong year, not the weekday.) analyze_captures.py clock, decrypt 8 Is 0x16 encrypted? Legacy S2M and SC route 0x16/0x23 to the XOR decoder. No. 0x16/0x17/0x23 are the plaintext Jacuzzi protocol; the J235 does not use them. The rewrite does not decode them as encrypted. PJ L1617–1665; HJ upstream removal 9 ClearRay code. PJ docs 0x0E; HJ/JB 0x0F. 0x0F (two independent sources; PJ text is internally inconsistent). Not exposed until confirmed on J235. protocol.md §3.3 10 Status cadence. "About every minute" (issue paraphrase) vs "very high rate" (PJ). ≈ 3.3 Hz on J235. D7: 1 804 C4 in 541 s; D2: 200 rows per full minute 12 Pump bits. Legacy definition: main pump = d2 bit 4, secondary = d1 bit 2, circulation = d1 bit 6. PJ: pump 1 is 2 bits. All three legacy bits are right, but their meaning is narrower: d1.6 = pump 1 running (any speed); d2 bits 4–3 = pump 1 speed (bit 4 = high); d1.2 = pump 2. D7 t≈90–196 13 Light codes. HJ: 0xF1 light on, 0xF2 colour. The J235 topside has one light button that sends 0x12 (HJ 0xF2) and steps through the modes. 0x11 is never sent. D7 t≈294–414 14 First temp press. Legacy: N presses for N half-degrees. The first press only enters set mode (d2 bit 5, d13 0x98). The legacy controller was always one press short. D7 t≈210, 238 16 Fold vs per byte. spa2mqtt 2.0 and HJ decode with the fold; HJ DECODING.md §3.8 asks whether the first byte of each pair is a key, a nonce or a second data channel. Answered with raw captures: payload[0] is a per-frame nonce, and after removing it both bytes of a pair can carry data. Decoding now removes the nonce and a key stream (pyjacuzzi's formula with four corrections) and reads plaintext per byte. It fixes the August–December date and the year on foreign frames, and it is shared with the Sundance 780. protocol.md §3.3; analyze_captures.py decrypt 15 Dormant channel reuse. HJ/IR rely on it. Not possible on this install: the only polled channel (0x10, the topside) answers every CTS. A client must use the 0x00/0x01 request. D7 census 11 decoding.md decoded values. The doc's "post-decoding" lines all show minute 0x26. The first 18 frames actually decode to minute 0x23; the doc copy-pasted the decode. Fixture keeps the raw frames, not the doc's decode. analyze_captures.py cipher

docs.title: The plain-protocol tub (Jacuzzi J345, November 2026)
docs.text:
The facts are in protocol-plain.md. This section records how they were settled.

Model name. The first outside definition (May 2025) and discussion 13 call the tub a "J335". That wording is srleach's, written before the owner's first reply. The owner wrote "J345" twice: "My tub is Jacuzzi J345 that's not encrypted using the original ProLink adapter" (discussion 6, 18 May 2025) and "unencrypted J345 (my tub)" (discussion 13, 10 December 2025). The definition is jacuzzi_j345. The legacy name jacuzzi_j335_unencrypted_farenheit is kept as an alias, because the owner's stack sets it.

Evidence base. Five logs from the owner (keys S, D, X1–X3 in protocol-plain.md §0). S is the important one: a pyjacuzzi session with 26 sent commands and the tub's reaction to each. D and X1–X3 are receive-only logs of topside actions. The pre-rewrite definition was not used: it read 0xC4 offsets and XOR constants on a board that sends 0x16 plaintext.

# Conflict or question Resolution Evidence P1 Indexing. PJ and JB index the whole frame; the definition indexes the payload. PJ data[n] is payload byte n − 5. Every PJ line cited in the definition was re-read with that offset. PJ jacuzzi.py L857–868 against S L5 P2 Heater. PJ reads heat state from p[5] bits 5–4; they are always 0 on this tub. The only heater candidate is p[11] bit 0, which follows the thermostat in three captures. Status: hypothesis. PJ L965 labels those bits "isUVOn". D L143; X3 L1299; S L11, L14 P3 How to get a turn to send. JB waits for a CTS on its channel; PJ just writes. The ProLink stream has no CTS at all, and PJ's 26 writes all worked. The bridge uses a direct mode with spacing. The owner had reported that JB's project could read but not control. D, X1–X3 census; S; JB jacuzziRS485.py L200–205 P4 Setpoint path. The J235 steps with temp up/down presses. Those button codes (0x01, 0x02) were never seen on this tub. The direct set-temperature frame (0x20) was, three times. The definition has no temp buttons. S L8–L14 P5 Which light record. PJ's command writes four records; the topside writes one. Decode record 0, the one both change. Records 1–3 are undecoded. X2, X3; S L27

Reference drift. JB's head is now 1840e3c (7 November 2026); protocol.md cites 96f3172. HJ's repository is at 9a1df08 and has withdrawn its plain 0x16 support (DECODING.md §3.9). PJ is unchanged at f9d6022, whose parent is the 39c2834 commit that protocol.md mentions.

Open. The list is protocol-plain.md §8. The first three would be settled by the owner's first receive-only run and first transmit test: whether the connection check is needed, whether the decoded temperatures match the topside, and whether the heater bit is the heater.

docs.text: A receive-only capture using tools/capture.py, with labelled topside actions. The result is D7 (tests/fixtures/captures/raw/2026-11-04T220754Z_j235_labelled.log). A follow-up capture reading the maintenance reminder values from the menu would close question 3.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: Read this page before you wire anything into a spa, and again before you enable transmit.

docs.title: Electrical safety
docs.text:
Mains voltage and water

A spa controller runs on mains voltage and can deliver a large fault current. Water makes a shock more likely and more severe.

  • Isolate the spa before you open it. Switch off the spa's breaker or isolator at the supply, not only at the topside. The topside does not disconnect mains from the board.
  • Check that it is dead. Use a suitable voltage tester before you touch anything in the control box.
  • Use only the RS485 header. The header on the control board is intended for a second topside panel. Do not take power or signals from any other point on the board.
  • Keep low-voltage parts dry and fixed. Mount the adapter or ESP32 in an enclosure, away from water and away from mains terminals. Route the bus cable so that it cannot touch mains parts.
  • Follow local rules. In many countries, work inside fixed mains equipment needs a qualified electrician. If you are not sure, ask one.
  • Your risk. Wiring anything into a spa is at your own risk. This project gives no warranty.

docs.title: Receive-only by default
docs.text:
Both the MQTT bridge and the ESPHome component start with transmit off. With transmit off:

  • Nothing is ever written to the bus. The bridge, the monitor and the capture tool only listen.
  • Buttons and the temperature setpoint still appear in Home Assistant, so their identities stay the same. The MQTT bridge shows them as unavailable. ESPHome logs a warning when you press one.
  • A wrong setting or a wrong tub definition can show wrong values. It cannot change the tub.

You enable transmit on purpose, with SPA_TRANSMIT=true or spa.transmit: true for the bridge, or transmit: true in the ESPHome spa_bus: block.

The read-only tools never transmit, whatever the setting:

  • spa2mqtt monitor runs receive-only and wraps its connection so that any write fails.
  • spa2mqtt replay reads a file and has no bus at all.
  • tools/capture.py contains no send call.

docs.title: One choke point for every write
docs.text:
Every write to the bus goes through one function:

  • Python: BusWriter.send() in spa2mqtt/tub/bus.py.
  • ESPHome: SpaBus::transmit_frame_() in esphome/components/spa_bus/spa_bus.cpp.

Each is marked TRANSMITS in the source. A test asserts that no other Python module writes to the transport. If transmit is off, the Python writer raises an error and the C++ function returns before it writes. One choke point makes the transmit path easy to review: you check one function, not the whole code base.

docs.title: What enabling transmit does
docs.text:
When you enable transmit:

  1. At start-up, nothing changes on the bus. The bridge logs TRANSMIT ENABLED, and the command entities become available in Home Assistant.
  2. On the first command from Home Assistant, the bridge claims a client channel on the bus. It does this the same way a second topside panel does: it takes a polled channel that no device uses, or it asks the board for a new channel and acknowledges the answer. From then on, the board polls that channel.
  3. When the board polls the channel, the bridge sends one queued button press. When nothing is queued, it stays silent.
  4. A setpoint change is a series of single up or down presses. After each press the bridge waits for status frames that confirm the change, and it gives up after a fixed number of attempts.
  5. If another device answers on the same channel, the bridge sees the conflict and goes back to listening.

The v1 bridge claimed a channel at start-up even when no one pressed a button. Version 2 does not.

The transmit path is tested against a simulated board, and runs on the project's own J235 through the MQTT bridge: the board granted channel 0x11 (protocol.md, D8). Watch the first commands at the topside of your own tub.

docs.title: Direct mode (Jacuzzi J345 through a ProLink module)
docs.text:
The J345 definition uses bus.mode: direct. The ProLink's TCP stream carries no polls, so there is no channel to claim. When you enable transmit:

  1. At start-up and on every reconnect, nothing is sent.
  2. On the first command after each connection, the bridge sends one connection-check frame (type 0x19). pyjacuzzi sends the same frame first. Whether the tub needs it is unknown.
  3. Each command is one frame, sent from the ProLink's own bus address (0x0A). Frames are at least four status frames apart, about 1.2 seconds.
  4. A setpoint change is a single set-temperature frame with the target in whole °F. The bridge refuses a target outside 80–104 °F. It does not clamp it. The setpoint is also blocked while the tub reports Celsius mode, and until the first status frame is decoded: in Celsius mode the same byte would mean half degrees Celsius.
  5. Nothing is retried. At most eight commands wait in the queue, and a reconnect drops them.

Every frame this mode can send is a frame that pyjacuzzi sent to the owner's tub in a captured session, reproduced byte for byte, with one exception: setpoints other than 90, 100 and 101 °F use the same frame with another value. A test enumerates every frame the definition can emit and fails if any other appears. The project has not run this path against the tub. See the J345 guide for the order of first tests.

docs.title: Rules for testing
docs.text:
• Never leave transmit on while you test an unknown or changed tub definition. A wrong button code, bus address or channel setting could send a command that you did not intend, or disturb the topside panel's own traffic. Test with transmit off until every value matches the topside.
  • Test new definitions with spa2mqtt monitor and replayed captures first. See Monitor and capture.
  • Enable transmit when someone can watch the topside. Press one button at a time and check the result.
  • If anything unexpected happens, set transmit off again and restart. If the topside shows an error, isolate the spa at the breaker and wait before you switch it on again.
  • Do not automate heating or pumps from Home Assistant until manual commands have worked reliably for some time.

docs.title: Tub definitions
docs.text:
A tub definition is a YAML file that describes one tub model. It says how to decode the status frames, which buttons exist, and which entities Home Assistant gets. The Python bridge reads it at start-up. The ESPHome component reads it at compile time and turns it into C++ tables. Because both read the same file, both give the same entities.

Built-in definitions live in definitions/. List them with:

spa2mqtt definitions

A new tub that uses an existing protocol family needs only a new YAML file, with no Python or C++. A tub with a different framing or cipher needs a new codec in spa2mqtt/protocol/ and in esphome/components/spa_bus/spa_protocol.cpp.

protocol Boards Runs on Reference balboa_encrypted Encrypted Jacuzzi and Sundance boards (0xC4 status), for example the J235 MQTT bridge and ESPHome Wire protocol jacuzzi_plain Unencrypted Jacuzzi boards (0x16 status) behind a ProLink module, for example the J345 MQTT bridge only Wire protocol (plain boards)

docs.title: Add a tub
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Capture with labels] --> B[Write definition YAML]
    B --> C[spa2mqtt validate]
    C --> D[Replay the capture<br/>and compare]
    D -->|values wrong| B
    D -->|values right| E[Generate ESPHome package]
    E --> F[Pull request]
  1. Capture. Record the bus with tools/capture.py while you press each topside button, and type a label before each press. See Monitor and capture.
  2. Copy a definition. Start from definitions/jacuzzi_j235.yaml. Give the copy a new id and file name.
  3. Edit the field map, buttons and entities. The sections below explain each part.

  4. Validate. spa2mqtt validate checks every definition against the schema and the loader's own checks. Give a path to check only your file:

    spa2mqtt validate definitions/my_tub.yaml

  5. Replay and compare. Decode your capture with your definition, and compare the values with what the topside showed at each label:

    spa2mqtt monitor --replay my-capture.log -d definitions/my_tub.yaml --describe

  6. Add tests. Put the capture in tests/fixtures/captures/raw/ and add the expected values to tests/test_replay.py. The tests then guard your definition from future changes. raw/ is for balboa_encrypted tubs: every capture there is also decoded by the C++ core with the J235 definition. Captures of other families go in their own folder, as the J345's do in tests/fixtures/captures/unencrypted/.

  7. Generate the ESPHome package. This writes esphome/packages/<id>.yaml with every entity of the definition:

    python3 tools/gen_esphome_package.py

    CI runs python3 tools/gen_esphome_package.py --check and fails if a package is out of date. Never edit a generated package by hand. The tool skips jacuzzi_plain definitions, because the ESPHome component does not implement that family.

  8. Open a pull request.

You can also use a definition file without adding it to the repository. Set spa.definition (or SPA_DEFINITION) to the file path for the bridge, or set definition: to the path in the ESPHome spa_bus: block.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text: The schema is definitions/tub-definition.schema.json (JSON Schema draft 2020-12). It documents every key. The loader adds checks that a schema cannot express: referenced fields and buttons exist, byte offsets fit in the payload, and keys are unique.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Key Meaning schema_version Always 1 id Lower-case identifier, for example jacuzzi_j235. Used in config and in topics aliases Other names that also select this definition name, manufacturer, model, description Shown in Home Assistant and in logs protocol Codec family in code: balboa_encrypted or jacuzzi_plain temperature_unit C or F. An entity with device_class: temperature must use the same unit ha Optional. device_name and device_identifier for Home Assistant, used when config.yml sets neither. Defaults: name and id bus Bus settings: baud, client_mid, channel_request_magic, dormant_channel_threshold. The last three are used only when transmit is on. See also Direct bus mode status How to decode the status frame. See Decode modes extra_frames Further periodic frames that fields may read. See Extra frames commands Button frame type, encoding (cc_xor or plain), the code of each button, and direct commands fields The field map. See Fields entities What Home Assistant gets. See Entities

docs.title: Decode modes
docs.text:
status.decode selects how the bridge turns a raw status frame into plain bytes. The encrypted boards hide the status payload with a per-frame key and a fixed key stream. See the wire protocol for the details.

Mode What it does Use it when decrypt Removes the per-frame key and the key stream. Every field then reads as plain bytes You know the key stream. This is the current J235 decode unkey Removes only the per-frame key You are still working out the key stream fold The older pairwise reading of the payload You have only old fold-based notes or logs plain Nothing. The payload is already plain bytes The board is unencrypted (protocol: jacuzzi_plain). The loader rejects it for any other family

status.length is the decoded length: 33 for decrypt and unkey on the J235, 16 for fold.

docs.title: Keystream
docs.text:
decrypt needs status.keystream. Byte i of the key stream (for i >= 1) is:

S[i] = xor ^ ((start - i + adjust[i]) mod 64)

xor and start are numbers. adjust is an optional map from byte index to a small correction. The J235 uses {xor: 0x19, start: 31, adjust: {"5": -8, "14": -8, "15": -8, "22": -8}}. The corrections were calibrated against the wall clock and the topside readings.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Each field reads a value from the decoded payload:

fields:
  water_temperature: {byte: 10, scale: 0.5, status: confirmed, evidence: "protocol.md §5 d5"}
  heater:            {byte: 21, bit: 6, status: confirmed}
  pump_1_speed:      {byte: 5, shift: 3, mask: 0x03, map: {"0": "off", "1": "low", "2": "high"}, status: confirmed}

The bridge and the ESPHome component apply the same steps, in this order:

  1. Read length bytes (default 1) from byte as a big-endian number.
  2. XOR the number with xor (default 0).
  3. If bit is set, the value is that bit, as on or off. Stop.
  4. Shift right by shift (default 0) and apply mask (default all ones).
  5. If the result is in invalid, the value is unknown.
  6. If map is set, the value is the mapped text. An unknown number gives an unknown value.
  7. Otherwise the value is raw * scale + offset (defaults 1 and 0).

Every field needs a status: confirmed, inferred or hypothesis. Add evidence to say where the claim comes from. The monitor shows the status next to each value, and the bridge logs entities that rest on a hypothesis.

docs.title: Extra frames
docs.text:
A plain board sends its light state in a second periodic frame. extra_frames names such a frame, and a field selects it with frame:

extra_frames:
  lights: {type: 0x23, length: 28}
fields:
  light_brightness: {frame: lights, byte: 2, status: confirmed, evidence: "S L63->L64"}

A field without frame reads the status frame. The loader checks the byte offset against the length of the frame the field names. Values from an extra frame merge into the same state as the status values.

On an encrypted board (balboa_encrypted) an extra frame is keyed, so it needs decode: fold. Fields then index the folded payload, d[j] = p[2j] ^ p[2j+1] ^ 1, which is length // 2 bytes long. The J235 lights frame:

extra_frames:
  lights: {type: 0xCA, length: 29, decode: fold}
fields:
  light_on: {frame: lights, byte: 1, bit: 6, status: confirmed, evidence: "D7 t~294 on, 307 off"}

decode: plain (the default) is for jacuzzi_plain only. The ESPHome component decodes the status frame only: its package leaves out entities that read an extra frame.

docs.title: Buttons and direct commands
docs.text:
commands.buttons maps a button name to its one-byte code. The short form is the code alone. The long form adds a status and evidence, and is the form to use for a tub that nobody on the project can test:

commands:
  type: 0x17
  encode: plain
  buttons:
    pump_1: {code: 0x04, status: confirmed, evidence: "S L22->L23 on, L24->L25 off"}

docs.title: Direct commands
docs.text:
commands.direct (jacuzzi_plain only) names commands that have their own frame type. The payload is a list of bytes. At most one item may be the word value, and then min and max give the allowed range of that byte:

  direct:
    set_temperature: {type: 0x20, payload: [value], min: 80, max: 104, status: confirmed, evidence: "S L8->L9"}
    light_red:       {type: 0x21, payload: [0x1F, 0x06, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0xFF, 0], status: confirmed, evidence: "S L38->L39"}

A button entity may press a direct command that has no value. A number entity uses one that has a value (see Entities). The bridge refuses to build a frame with a value outside min..max. Every direct command needs a status.

requires is an optional guard. It maps status bit fields to the value each must have in the last decoded status frame. If one differs, or no status frame has been decoded yet, the bridge refuses the command. The J345 uses requires: {celsius_mode: false} on set_temperature, because the byte it sends is only known to mean whole degrees Fahrenheit.

docs.title: Direct bus mode
docs.text:
bus.mode selects how the bridge gets its turn to send.

bus.mode Behaviour Use it when claim (default) Wait for the board's clear-to-send on a claimed channel (wire protocol §4) The bridge is on the RS485 bus itself (EW11A, USB adapter) direct Send from the fixed bus.client_address, one frame per bus.send_gap_frames status frames (default 4). No channel claim A module such as the ProLink arbitrates the bus (jacuzzi_plain only)

bus.hello names a direct command that the bridge sends once per connection, just before the first queued command. Leave it out to send no such frame. The loader requires commands.encode: plain and bus.mode: direct together.

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Each entity maps a field or a button to a Home Assistant entity.

component Needs Notes sensor field Optional device_class, unit_of_measurement, state_class, accuracy_decimals binary_sensor field Optional device_class text_sensor field For mapped values such as pump speed. Home Assistant shows it as a sensor with a text value button press A button name from commands.buttons, or a direct command with no value switch field, press An on/off state that a toggle button changes. field is a bit field. Optional off_field, confirm_frames, max_presses, progress_field, device_class. Bridge only number field, control, min, max, step control: {type: stepper, up:, down:} presses the up and down buttons until the field matches. control: {type: direct, command:} sends one direct command with the value

A direct number needs a one-byte field with no scale, offset, xor, shift or mask, whole-number min, max and step, and a range inside the command's min..max. The value sent is then the value shown. A value outside min..max is refused, not clamped: one message becomes one frame, with no stepping.

A switch presses its button only while field differs from the state that Home Assistant asked for. After each press it waits confirm_frames status frames (default 10, about three seconds on a J235) for the field to follow, then presses again. It stops after max_presses (default 3) and logs a warning. The wait matters: a second press sent too early turns a two-state pump straight back.

Some pumps cycle off, low, high, off, so "off" from low takes two presses and the field stays on in between. Name the speed field as progress_field. A change there shows that the press arrived, and the next press follows without the wait.

A switch for one speed of such a pump reads that speed's bit, but its "off" should be the pump fully off, not the next speed. Name the "running at any speed" bit as off_field: "off" is then reached when that field reads false. The J235 Pump 1 Low switch reads pump_1_low and has off_field: pump_1_running, so turning it off from low steps through high to off.

With bus.mode: direct a switch sends one frame and never retries, so max_presses must be 1 (the default there).

The ESPHome component has no switch platform yet. The generated package leaves switches out.

Every entity has a key, a component and a name. Optional: icon (mdi:...), entity_category (diagnostic or config), enabled_by_default, description.

Keys and names are identities

The key becomes the Home Assistant unique_id. With legacy topics on, the name is part of the discovery topic. Changing either one for an existing tub creates a new entity in Home Assistant and leaves the old one behind.

docs.title: Test a new definition safely
docs.text: Keep transmit off while you test a new or changed definition. A wrong field map only shows wrong values. A wrong button code or bus setting with transmit on could send a command that you did not intend. See Safety.

docs.title: ESPHome component
docs.text:
spa_bus is an ESPHome external component. An external component is ESPHome code that lives outside the ESPHome project and that ESPHome downloads when it compiles your device. spa_bus runs the spa2mqtt decoder directly on an ESP32 that is wired to the tub's RS485 bus. RS485 is the two-wire serial bus that the tub's control board uses to talk to its topside panel.

The ESP32 reads the status that the control board broadcasts about three times per second. It decodes the status and publishes it to Home Assistant through the ESPHome native API. The native API is the direct, encrypted link between an ESPHome device and Home Assistant.

docs.title: Why run it on ESPHome
docs.text:
The MQTT bridge needs three parts between the tub and Home Assistant: an RS485-to-TCP adapter such as the EW11A, a Docker host, and an MQTT broker. The ESPHome component replaces all three with one ESP32.

  • No adapter box and no vendor cloud. The ESP32's own UART reads the bus. A UART is the serial port on the chip. Nothing depends on an adapter's firmware or app.
  • No MQTT broker. Home Assistant discovers the device through the ESPHome integration. Entities appear in Home Assistant with no discovery topics to manage.
  • Fewer moving parts. One device to power, update and back up. ESPHome updates it over the air.

The MQTT bridge is still the better choice when you already have an RS485-to-TCP adapter installed, or when you want the monitor and replay tools. See Getting started for the comparison.

docs.title: One set of tub definitions
docs.text:
A tub definition is a YAML file in the repository's definitions/ folder. It describes one tub model: where each value sits in the status frame, the button codes, and the Home Assistant entities. The Python bridge reads the same files at run time.

The ESPHome component reads the definition at compile time. ESPHome downloads the whole repository for the external component, so the component's Python code can open definitions/<name>.yaml. It validates the file, then generates C++ code that loads the field table and button codes into the firmware. This process is called code generation (codegen).

The result:

  • A new tub needs a new definition file. It needs no new C++.
  • A fix in a definition reaches both the bridge and the ESP32 at the next release.
  • Each ESPHome entity names a definition entity with an entity: key. ESPHome checks at compile time that the key exists and that it has the right type, so a typo stops the build instead of producing a dead entity.

See Tub definitions for the file format.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Decodes the Jacuzzi J235 status: water temperature, setpoint, pump states, heater, set mode and diagnostics.
  • A ready-made package lists every J235 entity. A package is an ESPHome YAML file that you include in your own device file. You can also choose entities one at a time.
  • A bus_state diagnostic sensor shows whether status frames arrive and, with transmit on, the state of the bus channel.
  • Publishes each value when it changes, plus a heartbeat every 60 s so Home Assistant always holds a current value.
  • Receive-only by default. The component sends nothing to the tub until you set transmit: true.
  • With transmit on: topside button presses (temperature up and down, pumps, light) and a setpoint number that steps the temperature to a target.
  • Optional flow_control_pin for RS485 transceivers that need a direction pin.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Transmit is not tested on a real tub

The transmit path works against a simulated control board in the test suite. Nobody has yet tested it against a real J235. Leave transmit: false unless you want to help test it, and watch the tub when you first send a command.

  • While transmit: false, the buttons and the setpoint number still appear in Home Assistant. They do nothing when you use them. The ESP32 logs a warning such as transmit disabled (spa_bus.transmit: false); ignoring press 0x01.
  • One spa_bus hub per device. One ESP32 serves one tub.
  • The component supports the "encrypted" Balboa-family protocol only. Boards with a different framing need a new codec. See the wire protocol.
  • Only the J235 has an ESPHome definition today. jacuzzi_j345 (an unencrypted board behind a ProLink module) is for the MQTT bridge only: the component refuses it at compile time with a message that starts protocol 'jacuzzi_plain' not supported by spa_bus, and no package is generated for it.
